jobs.description:
Mission – Why we exist, what we do, and why we need you

SpotMe is a leading B2B event platform that helps enterprises increase the impact of their events by delivering CRM-connected, high-quality experiences across in-person, virtual, hybrid events, and webinars. With a strong focus on life sciences, SpotMe powers Onomi: an HCP engagement product that enables medical and commercial teams to run impactful congresses, symposia, advisory boards, and webinars. Together, SpotMe and Onomi turn events into a company’s most effective engagement channel.

This position is the ideal role for experienced talents in tech/services sales. With a self-driven resilient mindset, positive energy, and strong business acumen, you'll thrive in a fast paced environment. You will negotiate multi-year enterprise contracts, drive revenue and usage growth across our largest Fortune 500 accounts, and shape the long-term success of our most valued partnerships. Our top-performing Account Directors typically progress to sales leadership roles.

The Account Director role is key in our sales team and reports directly to the VP of Account Management. Following our Onomi launch, life sciences expansion pipeline is the #1 company objective, and driving revenue growth within existing customers is a key component.

As the account leader, you will be the primary point of contact for 7-15 key accounts with a total revenue of ~$3M and:

  • [40%] Identify and close expansion, upgrade and renewal opportunities.
  • [20%] Account retention and expansion plan execution: inserting Onomi into centers of excellence and delivery units, designing operating procedures for flawless execution, coordinating implementation and key integrations, evangelizing buying centers, functions and geo/affiliates with workshops and webinars, and partner engagement, briefing and certification.
  • [15%] Build relationships with key account stakeholders: engaging with new users, fostering trust-based relationships with champions and above-event stakeholders (commercial excellence, medical, IT, procurement), establishing open lines of communication with economic buyers, influencing HQ-prescribed technology usage guidelines, facilitating introductions and exec touchpoints at director/VP level with a meaningful briefing, demonstrating value in absolute ROI terms, and securing customer presence at customer advisory boards and 3rd-party events and roundtables.
  • [10%] Perform account research, mapping and planning: capturing intelligence on organization design, strategic priorities, Onomi's share of wallet, other vendors' scope, and integration, usage and investments for each use case; understanding budget cycles; partner mapping; and creating pricing benchmarks against other solutions.
  • [10%] Handle first-line account compliance, administrative and product inquiries.
  • [5%] Report on sales activities: CRM updates, sales forecasts and pipeline calls.

Objectives - The problems you will solve

In your first 1 month, you will:

  • Join our leadership team at live industry events: staff the booth at tradeshows and walk congresses with them
  • Master our core sales plays: rehearse them, listen to past winning calls, and successfully conduct an expansion mock demo call that convinces the team you can do it alone
  • Master our sales processes and systems (Salesforce, Google Suite, PowerPoint, Fathom) to be able to manage a sales lifecycle from customer request to contract expansion deals autonomously
  • Get introduced to all customers in your portfolio and secure face time with 80% of them.

In your first 3 months, you will:

  • Close your first deal autonomously
  • Identify 2 expansion levers for each account, with goals and steps documented in Salesforce
  • Attend your first congress solo, with a pre-event target list, a floor contact log, and 100% follow-up
  • Complete your account research and planning for every account in your portfolio, including renewal strategy and budget insertion

After the first 6 months, key indicators (usage and logo revenue) are trending up

After 12 months, you will:

  • Have met 100% of your customer portfolio in person at least once and met 1-3 new influential stakeholders per account
  • Have executed your account plans and achieved an aggregate 20% YoY revenue growth on your portfolio through services and/or software expansion

What you need to be great at:

  • Account leadership: You are above all a true account leader in B2B SaaS or services/consulting - you have managed large accounts ($200K-$2M) in large companies (>500 employees) over time, and you are able to truly understand the decision-making process and buying centers, and establish and nurture relationships with key people to expand scope and volume. You know what it means to operate a global, large-scale account in a first-class fashion.
  • Industry expertise with business orientation: You bring experience selling into or leading accounts in critical industries (pharma, financial services, professional services, or tech), whether at a SaaS company, an agency, or a consultancy, with a track record of working with the most demanding customers. Above all, you have a flair for spotting pain points, helping customers form business cases, and guiding them toward execution. Pharma HCP engagement expertise, with all its nuances (medical, commercial, marketing), is a plus but not a must.
  • Autonomy and resourcefulness: You create your own pipeline rather than waiting for deals to arrive, and you'll happily staff a congress booth solo for three days to do it. You make decisions with confidence and don't wait to be told what to do. When you hit a wall, you find a way around it. You're scrappy, creative, and solution-oriented by nature, and you act proactively even when there's no immediate commercial upside.
  • Commercial sharpness: You run numbers quickly, think several steps ahead in negotiations, and understand what truly drives your customers' business. You can build a solid business case that holds up in front of a C-suite or procurement team, and you are comfortable making decisions and forming working hypotheses even when you don't have all the facts.
  • Customer and product depth: You want to understand why a customer's organization works the way it does: how decisions get made, where the friction sits, and what sits beneath the stated need. You know the product well enough to handle the hard questions yourself and shape a solution in the room, bringing in specialists when they add something you can't, not as a substitute for knowing the answer.
  • Coachability at speed: We invest heavily in coaching, and we look for people who welcome it at any stage of their career. You take direct feedback without defensiveness, and what we sharpen with you one day shows up in your next customer conversation.

SpotMe recruits, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, parental status, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care.
jobs.description:
Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. For Life Sciences partners, we offer the leading at-home EEG platform for clinical development of novel therapeutics for neurological, psychiatric, and sleep disorders. Our Diagnostics business is building the most comprehensive at-home platform for precision diagnostics, combining EEG and cardiopulmonary signals to deliver reimbursable assessments for sleep and central nervous system disorders. Together, we're changing the way patients are diagnosed and treated for any disorder that affects brain physiology.

Beacon Biosignals is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to join our Datastore team. The Datastore sits at the heart of Beacon's platform. It defines our foundational data model and serves as the centralized repository and API for brain data collected from clinical studies, supporting the analytical tools, services, and applications used by our scientists, clinicians, and partners.

This role emphasizes the design and scaling of backend systems for data infrastructure: PostgreSQL data models, Kafka-driven event pipelines, and the GraphQL API that makes scientific and clinical data usable - distinct from frontend development or end-user product surfaces. At this level you will lead the design of complex systems within the Datastore rather than individual components, own the pipelines that deliver dataset snapshots into our warehouse, and collaborate across platform, application and scientific teams to implement APIs that unlock new workflows in Beacon's expanding portfolio of clinical studies and digital health products.

You should have experience writing complex SQL queries by hand, and should be prepared to reason about schema design, indexes, and query behavior as a matter of course.

Two properties of our system that shape our work may influence your application. Our GraphQL API is generated from the PostgreSQL schema using PostGraphile, so a schema decision is an API decision. Secondly, row-level security is in force on effectively every table, because clinical data from different studies and partners shares one schema, with some rows shared for access by multiple internal teams. RLS predicates get injected into your queries, which makes reasoning about query plans genuinely harder here than it is in most places. If that sounds interesting rather than tedious, you'll enjoy this team.

We are hiring two engineers into this role, with two different centers of gravity. One will focus on the breadth of the Datastore: the event pipelines, the GraphQL API, core data models, and third-party integrations. The other will focus on depth in PostgreSQL (data modeling, performance tuning, operations) and supporting all engineers in developing schemas and the access controls that protect clinical data. The core requirements are the same. Tell us which one you are most drawn to in your application.

This role is 100% remote from anywhere in the U.S. Beacon's robust asynchronous work practices ensure a first-class remote work experience, but we also have in-person office hubs in Boston, New York City, and Paris.

What success looks like

  • You lead design and architecture for complex projects and systems within the Datastore, weighing implementation trade-offs with engineering principles and backing your decisions with data rather than preference
  • You partner with product managers, scientific and clinical stakeholders, and other development and support teams to translate their requirements into new integrations, services, and solutions for scaling Beacon's data platform - contributing to broader product and technical decisions, not simply implementing them
  • You debug and profile ambiguous problems that cross system boundaries, including codebases beyond the Datastore's purview, and you leave what you touch better than you found it — structure, test coverage, tooling
  • Peers look to your work as an example: you implement features with attention to detail, demonstrating product awareness and high standards for data integrity, design soundness, and maintainability across the lifespan of the system
  • You draft RFCs to lead complex feature discovery and technical design phases, soliciting and incorporating input, and helping your team align on a set of decisions to guide development
  • You plan your own work and contribute to planning the team's, making reasoned trade-offs between speed, generalizability, and technical debt, and accounting for the needs of multiple stakeholder teams
  • You teach and mentor other engineers regularly, give feedback that people act on, and are sought out for it. You may act as tech lead on a project or as the coordination point for engineering practice within the team
  • You leverage feedback from internal stakeholders and external partners to improve operational robustness and ease of use of the Datastore and its services via new documentation, tools, and dashboards

What you will bring

  • 7+ years of backend development experience, including at least 3 years focused on data platforms and backend infrastructure for data-centric applications: transactional systems, event pipelines, and the APIs that serve them
  • Highly proficient in at least one technical area relevant to this work: data modeling, distributed systems, API design, or database engineering, with the depth that others on a team come to you for
  • Strong proficiency in SQL, with production experience working with PostgreSQL as an application database; you write and tune queries fluently and are comfortable reasoning about schema design, indexes, and query plans
  • Hands-on experience with data streaming and event processing, using Kafka (our event bus) or an equivalent such as RabbitMQ, Pulsar, or a cloud-based equivalent like Amazon Kinesis
  • Proficiency in Julia or Python; Julia is a core Datastore language, and experience with Julia is a strong plus, but not required — we welcome candidates eager to learn it!
  • Experience deploying and operating services in containerized environments, with familiarity in Kubernetes and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform and/or Helm
  • A track record of mentoring engineers and improving how a team works - practices, tooling, test coverage, or documentation that outlasted your involvement
  • A collaborative mindset: you enjoy working across disciplines and believe people achieve more together than alone
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially in asynchronous and remote-friendly environments
  • A self-directed approach, with a track record of thriving in hybrid or fully remote teams
  • Experience with, or interest in, using LLM-assisted or agentic coding tools in a production setting, with good judgment about what guardrails are needed

For the Datastore Systems role:

  • You can lead design across the breadth of the platform.
  • GraphQL and TypeScript/JavaScript (Node.js) - GraphQL is the Datastore's primary interface, and this profile owns significant parts of it
  • Designing event-driven pipelines end to end: producers, consumers, replay, idempotency, and what happens when a consumer falls behind
  • Leading the design of complex systems rather than individual components, across the API, the pipelines, and the services that depend on them

For the PostgreSQL & Data Modeling role:

  • You can be the person the rest of the team comes to about the database.
  • Deep PostgreSQL: you reason fluently about the query planner, index selection, and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE), and why a query that should be fast isn't
  • Data modeling: you design the schema itself: entities, relationships, and the constraints that make invalid states impossible. Including how to model time, since clinical results get re-scored and corrected and we need to answer "what did this look like when the report was signed?"
  • Schema evolution under load: zero-downtime migrations, dual-write transitions, lock avoidance, backfill and verification. Our schema has hundreds of migrations behind it and will have hundreds more
  • Operating PostgreSQL in production, not only designing for it: upgrades, replication, backup and restore, connection pooling, bloat and vacuum behaviour, extensions
  • Making others good at it: you teach, review, and document, because a schema only stays coherent if the team understands it

We don't expect every candidate to check every box. If you bring strong fundamentals, care about data infrastructure for health, and are excited to learn, we’d love to hear from you!

The US-based salary range for this role is $170,000 – $190,000. Salary ranges are determined using current market compensation data for this role and adjusted based on experience, skills, and location. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes equity, PTO and other benefits.

At Beacon, we've found that cultural and scientific impact is driven most by those that lead by example. As such, we're always seeking new contributors whose work demonstrates an avid curiosity, a bias towards simplicity, an eye for composability, a self-service mindset, and - most of all - a deep empathy towards colleagues, stakeholders, users, and patients. We believe a diverse team builds more robust systems and achieves higher impact.

jobs.description:
Executive Director, California College Guidance Initiative

100% Remote within California; must reside in California


The Foundation for California Community Colleges (FoundationCCC) is the official nonprofit auxiliary to the California Community Colleges, the largest and most diverse system of higher education in the nation. Founded in 1998, FoundationCCC has served as a catalyst for student success, workforce development, and community impact across California. The organization manages over 70 programs and initiatives that expand opportunity and accelerate pathways to economic and social mobility for all Californians — piloting new approaches, replicating promising practices, and scaling sustainable methods to support all 116 California community colleges and 2.2 million students.


Since its founding, FoundationCCC has delivered hundreds of millions in grants, support, and cost savings to colleges, and 86% of every dollar that comes into FoundationCCC directly supports programs and services that benefit the colleges and their students. FoundationCCC plays a pivotal role in forging new partnerships and accelerating bold approaches to advance the California Community Colleges and the communities they serve.


About CCGI

The California College Guidance Initiative (CCGI) manages CaliforniaColleges.edu, the state's official college and career planning platform. CCGI is a legislatively authorized service provider to all California school districts as established in California Education Code Section 60900.5. CaliforniaColleges.edu helps students explore college and career options, launch their college and financial aid applications, and access financial aid lessons, all on one site. It helps educators utilize data-driven guidance and streamline student support, while allowing parents and guardians to view and monitor their student's progress. By connecting information, planning, and application processes, CCGI strengthens college and career readiness and expands access to postsecondary opportunities statewide.


CCGI partners with K-12 school districts across the state to give students, families, and counselors the tools they need to ensure that all California students, especially those who have been underrepresented in higher education, can move seamlessly from K-12 to college and career. The organization serves more than 650 local educational agencies, transmitting transcript data, powering transcript-informed tools, and streamlining applications for college admissions and financial aid.


CCGI operates as a structurally embedded project under the fiscal sponsorship of FoundationCCC and is a Collaborative Impact Partner of the organization. This partnership allows CCGI to focus entirely on its data-driven mission to support California students while leveraging the robust administrative infrastructure of the community college system's official nonprofit partner. The fiscal partnership model reflects how FoundationCCC works across California's education landscape: incubating and scaling high-impact initiatives that strengthen the pipeline from K-12 into the California community colleges and beyond.

The organization employs roughly 80 staff distributed across four divisions: Programs, CaliforniaColleges.edu, Data and Strategy, and Operations, with regional teams spanning the state.


The Role

CCGI's next Executive Director will guide the organization's strategic direction, strengthen its statewide relationships, and oversee a leadership team accountable for delivering its mission and statutory responsibilities. This leader will connect education policy, partnerships, organizational resources, and execution to reduce barriers and expand students' access to college and career pathways. The role reports to FoundationCCC as the most senior CCGI leader and serves as CCGI's most critical and influential advocate with leadership at the state's public educational institutions, the state legislature, the Governor's office, and the Department of Finance.


What We Are Seeking


Strategic Direction and Execution

Sets clear priorities, articulates a compelling future for CCGI — expanding into areas like deepening platform adoption and leveraging data more powerfully — while simultaneously managing the practical realities of funding constraints, statutory compliance, and intersegmental coordination. Translates strategy into measurable outcomes and resource decisions and adjusts direction as student needs and statewide conditions evolve.


Statewide Relationship-Based Leadership

Builds and deepens trust across education systems and government partners — including 650+ K-12 Local Education Agencies, the California Department of Education, the California Community Colleges, California State University, the University of California, the California Student Aid Commission and the Cradle-to-Career Data System. Navigates competing priorities with diplomacy and develops coalitions that advance shared outcomes through influence rather than positional authority.


Team-Centered Stewardship

Honors the deep expertise of the existing team, provides clarity and resources so divisions can execute, builds strong retention, and enters the organization with humility. Leads through senior leaders, clarifies decision-making authority, strengthens accountability, and develops leadership capacity across the organization.


Financial and Organizational Stewardship

Accountable for both long-term financial sustainability through continued state funding, philanthropy funding opportunities, and cybersecurity and risk management


Student-Centered, Equity-Informed Judgment

Uses evidence and stakeholder perspectives to identify barriers and make decisions that improve educational access and opportunity — especially for students most harmed by misalignment between education systems.


Communication and Culture

Communicates clearly across audiences, welcomes constructive disagreement, provides direct and respectful feedback, and models collaboration, learning, and accountability.


Essential Responsibilities

MISSION AND STRATEGIC ALIGNMENT

  • Provides executive leadership to position CCGI to effectively achieve its mission, statutory responsibilities, and long-term strategic objectives.
  • Establishes CCGI's medium- and long-term strategic direction in alignment with its mission, statutory responsibilities, FoundationCCC's mission, and evolving statewide education priorities.
  • Translates strategic direction into clear annual and multi-year priorities, outcomes, and resource commitments.
  • Holds executive leaders accountable for organizational performance and uses data, results, and changing conditions to assess progress and adjust strategy.
  • Anticipates changes in the external environment and positions CCGI to respond effectively to emerging policy, funding, technology, and educational priorities.
  • Champions innovative, scalable solutions that reduce systemic barriers, lessen administrative burden, and improve student access to college and career pathways.

ORGANIZATIONAL STEWARDSHIP

  • Provides overall executive leadership, direction, and accountability for CCGI's strategy, operations, organizational performance, and impact.
  • Leads and supports CCGI's leadership team, providing direction and counsel to division leaders on strategic, financial, operational, and organizational decisions.
  • Establishes clear decision-making authority, accountability, and expectations across the executive team and organization.
  • Builds and develops a cohesive, high-performing leadership team capable of advancing shared priorities.
  • Ensures organizational structures, leadership capacity, systems, and resources support effective execution of CCGI's mission and strategy while maintaining alignment with FoundationCCC's mission.
  • Maintains an organizational culture grounded in CCGI's mission and values, reinforcing collaboration, accountability, innovation, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
  • Proactively oversees legal, financial, operational, cybersecurity, compliance, and reputational risk and ensures appropriate controls and practices are in place.

EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT

  • Serves as a principal executive representative for CCGI with education leaders, state officials, policymakers, partners, funders, and other key stakeholders.
  • Cultivates and sustains long-term strategic relationships with leaders and organizations across education segments, state agencies, governmental entities, and other key partners.
  • Builds and sustains strategic coalitions that strengthen alignment across education systems and advance CCGI's mission and statewide impact.
  • Exercises diplomacy, political acumen, and executive communication to navigate complex stakeholder environments and strengthen CCGI's visibility, credibility, and influence.
  • Leads the annual and multi-year budgeting process in coordination with the Department of Finance, Legislature, and other appropriate stakeholders.
  • Ensures CCGI fulfills its statutory purpose and responsibilities as established in California law and applicable state requirements.
  • Maintains executive accountability for legislative reporting, funding requirements, governmental commitments, and other state oversight obligations.
  • Ensures the Cradle-to-Career Data System Governing Board and other appropriate state constituents are informed of CCGI's work, priorities, progress, and significant organizational developments.

Experience and Knowledge

  • Organizational leadership — Experience leading a distributed team of 50+ through an executive leadership structure.  
  • Equity-centered strategy — Demonstrated ability to translate equity commitments into organizational policy, hiring, and partnerships. 
  • Government relations — Experience working with or within the Legislature, Governor's office, or Department of Finance on education policy or funding. 
  • California education ecosystem — Deep familiarity with K-12, community colleges, CSU, UC, and the state agencies that connect them. 
  • Government relations — Experience working with or within the Legislature, Governor's office, or Department of Finance on education policy or funding. 
  • Intersegmental/Cross-Sector coordination — Track record of building alignment across institutional boundaries with competing priorities. 
  • Organizational leadership — Experience leading a distributed team of 50+ through an executive leadership structure. 
  • Data-informed operations — Comfort with data systems, student data privacy and related legal requirements, and using evidence to drive strategy. 
  • Financial stewardship — Budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, and managing state funding relationships. 
  • Equity-centered strategy — Demonstrated ability to translate equity commitments into organizational policy, hiring, and partnerships. 
  • Nonprofit and public-sector context — Understanding regulatory compliance, contracting, and the constraints of operating as a public-facing nonprofit. 

Leadership Qualities

  • Integrity and trustworthiness — Authentic, transparent, and consistent in word and action.
  • Relationship-first approach — Builds coalition through genuine engagement, not positional authority.
  • Humility and curiosity — Enters with respect for what the team has built; listens before acting.
  • Political sophistication — Comfortable in ambiguity; reads institutional dynamics and acts accordingly.
  • Courageous advocacy — Willing to champion CCGI's mission and its team in high-stakes settings.
  • Communication clarity — Can articulate complex intersegmental work to legislators, educators, and students alike.
  • Vulnerability and self-reflection — Models the feedback culture CCGI values, including Nonviolent Communication.
  • Long-term commitment — Sees this as a calling, not a stepping stone.

Cultural Alignment

CCGI's team culture is built on nine characteristics that are deeply embedded in how the organization works. The next leader must not only endorse these qualities but model them daily:

Collaboration and learning · Data-driven practices · Direct feedback

Documentation · Due diligence and preparation · Professionalism and kindness

Self-reflection · Strategic thinking · Vulnerability

The Executive Director sets the tone for this culture and is expected to model, provide, and receive feedback using the Nonviolent Communication framework.

What we Offer

FoundationCCC is fully committed to a “remote-first” philosophy, and recruits and hires talent across the state in fully remote positions, where virtual work is possible. Our headquarters are located in Downtown Sacramento, just blocks from California’s State Capitol.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation, generous PTO, and paid holidays
  • Medical, dental, and vision plans, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts (HSA), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and Wellness offerings
  • CalPERS retirement program and optional 403(b) and 457 Retirement plans
  • Carrot reproductive health and fertility support
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness certified employer

Working Hours, Location, and Travel 

Hours: Full-time position, 40 hours per week, with additional hours needed to address the organization’s needs.

Location: California-based with the flexibility to work remotely (in California). 

Travel: Regular daytime travel and in-person attendance at events and meetings within the state to align with the needs of the institutions in the state. Overnight travel (up to 20%) by land and air.

jobs.description:
About the role

Agile Six is looking for a senior market development leader to grow our work across the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the broader U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the federal health information technology landscape.

We have more than a decade of delivery experience at CMS and HHS, including work in payment modernization, quality programs, agile transformation, and grants modernization. This role will build from that foundation, deepening our presence across CMS first, while identifying strategic opportunities across HHS and health IT where our experience and delivery model give us a meaningful advantage.

This is a highly autonomous role with significant responsibility for shaping where Agile Six invests, which opportunities we pursue, and how we develop relationships and partnerships in the market. As a self-managed organization, “Director” reflects the scope, accountability, and external leadership of the role rather than traditional people-management authority. Success is more than generating pipeline or revenue. We want to pursue work that aligns with our capabilities, values, and ability to deliver meaningful outcomes for government partners.

What you'll do

Develop and execute our CMS/HHS market strategy

  • Build and maintain a clear understanding of CMS centers and offices, decision-makers, modernization priorities, acquisition patterns, contract vehicles, incumbents, and upcoming opportunities.
  • Translate market intelligence into a prioritized strategy for where Agile Six should invest time, relationships, and pursuit resources.
  • Extend that strategy into adjacent HHS and health IT opportunities where our CMS experience creates a credible foundation.

Build relationships and shape opportunities

  • Develop trusted relationships with government leaders, industry partners, primes, and other stakeholders across CMS and HHS.
  • Represent Agile Six at relevant industry events, conferences, and partner conversations.
  • Identify opportunities early enough to help shape stronger solutions and acquisition approaches rather than simply responding to released solicitations.

Own and develop a qualified pipeline

  • Build and maintain a disciplined pipeline based on strategic fit, realistic win probability, delivery alignment, and potential impact.
  • Make thoughtful pursue/no-pursue recommendations and be willing to recommend walking away from work that is not right for Agile Six.
  • Connect pipeline planning with organizational forecasting and broader Market Development priorities.

Connect market development with delivery

  • Work closely with Agile Six delivery teams to understand our existing work, client needs, lessons learned, and potential areas for expansion.
  • Bring delivery expertise into opportunity shaping and ensure proposed work reflects what Agile Six can credibly and successfully deliver.
  • Help create relationships and opportunities that give future delivery teams a strong foundation for success.

Develop partnerships and solutions

  • Identify and develop teaming, subcontracting, and joint-venture opportunities that expand Agile Six's reach or capabilities.
  • Lead or support strategic partner and teaming negotiations while protecting the integrity of our delivery model.
  • Partner with Communications, Proposals, Delivery, Finance, Contracts, and company leadership throughout opportunity development and proposal work.

Strengthen how we do market development

  • Use AI-enabled tools to support research, market mapping, pipeline analysis, competitive intelligence, and opportunity development.
  • Contribute to shared Market Development practices, tools, intelligence, and strategy rather than operating as an individual sales function.
  • Help improve systems and practices that are still developing rather than waiting for perfect infrastructure.

What success looks like

In this role, you will:

  • Give Agile Six a substantially clearer view of the CMS market: where opportunities exist, where we have credibility, who we need to know, and where we should invest.
  • Build and deepen relationships across CMS centers and the broader HHS ecosystem that lead to qualified opportunities.
  • Develop a healthy pipeline of opportunities that balance growth potential with strategic and delivery fit.
  • Identify partnerships and teaming strategies that meaningfully expand Agile Six's ability to compete and deliver.
  • Help turn Agile Six's existing CMS/HHS delivery credibility into a larger, sustainable portfolio.
  • Strengthen the way Market Development and Delivery share intelligence and shape opportunities together.
  • Improve and make effective use of Agile Six's AI-enabled market development practices.

What we expect at this level

As a senior leader at Agile Six, you will be expected to:

  • Operate with significant autonomy and make sound decisions in areas where the path is not already defined.
  • Translate broad organizational goals into strategy, priorities, and measurable action.
  • Work effectively across organizational boundaries and influence outcomes without relying on positional authority.
  • Exercise judgment about where Agile Six should and should not invest.
  • Build alignment among people with different expertise, incentives, and perspectives.
  • Surface risks, gaps, and changing conditions early and recommend a path forward.
  • Strengthen organizational capability through what you build, learn, document, and share.
  • Represent Agile Six's values and interests thoughtfully in high-stakes external relationships.

What you'll bring

Required

  • Significant experience in business development, market development, partnerships, or a similar strategic role in federal technology, digital services, or consulting.
  • Deep familiarity with the CMS ecosystem, including how its centers operate, how technology services are procured, and the vehicles, partners, and incumbents that shape the market.
  • Working knowledge of the broader HHS landscape.
  • An established network within CMS and/or among organizations that work extensively with CMS.
  • Strong relationship-building and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to turn relationships and market knowledge into meaningful outcomes.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with delivery, contracts, finance, proposal, and/or other business functions.
  • Ability to evaluate opportunities strategically rather than simply maximize pipeline volume.
  • Experience using AI-enabled tools in your work, with sound judgment about where human expertise and context remain essential.
  • Comfort operating in a small, evolving organization where systems and processes may still be developing.

Helpful experience

  • Previous federal service at CMS or another HHS operating division.
  • Experience navigating CMS/HHS procurement and acquisition environments.
  • Familiarity with joint ventures, SDVOSB/8(a) partnerships, set-aside strategy, and federal teaming.
  • Experience with health IT domains such as quality measurement, payment modernization, interoperability, or grants.
  • Understanding of the relationship between federal health programs and state-level implementation.

How you'll work

Market Development at Agile Six is a team effort. You will own significant areas of strategy and pipeline, but you won't operate as an isolated salesperson. You'll work with company leadership, Market Development teammates, delivery teams, and organizational partners to bring the right expertise into opportunities at the right time.

Our strongest growth comes from work we understand and can deliver well. That means staying close to Delivery, sharing intelligence openly, and measuring success by the quality and impact of the work we win.

Employment & Compensation

Engagement: Full-time; open to W-2 employment or an initial contract-to-hire arrangement.
Compensation: Compensation will depend on the final level and engagement structure. For W-2 employment, Agile Six's current base salaries for the levels under consideration range from $182,767–$250,460. Contract compensation would be established separately based on the engagement structure.Location: US Remote. Preference will be given to candidates in the MD/N.VA/DC area.

Sixer Benefits

Our benefits are designed to reinforce our core values of Wholeness, Self Management and Inclusion. We respect that only you know what balance means for your life and season. While we offer support from coaches, we expect you to own your wholeness, show up for work whole, and go home to your family the same. You will be seen, heard and valued. We expect you to offer the same for your colleagues, be kind (not controlling), be caring (not directive) and ready to participate in a state of flow. We mean it when we say “We build better by putting people first”.

  • Self-managed work/life balance and flexibility
  • Competitive salary
  • Employee Stock Ownership (ESOP) for all employees!
  • 401(k) matching
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Employer paid short and long term disability insurance
  • Employer paid life insurance
  • Self-managed and generous paid time off
  • Paid federal holidays and two floating holidays
  • Paid parental leave
  • Self-managed professional development spending
  • Self-managed wellness days

Hiring practices

Agile Six is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any factor protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

Note: We participate in E-Verify. Upon hire, we will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. Unfortunately, we are unable to sponsor visas at this time.

If you need assistance or reasonable accommodation in applying for any of these positions, please reach out to . We want to ensure you have the ability to apply for any position at Agile Six.

Please read and respond to the application questions carefully. Interviews are conducted on a rolling basis until the position has been filled.

jobs.description:
Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Despite autism diagnoses increasing more than 5x in the past 25 years, autistic adults have been systematically overlooked. This has led to extremely poor outcomes, including high rates of co-occurring mental health conditions and a lower life expectancy. Prosper is here to change that.

We deliver specialized mental health services for autistic adults, covered by insurance. We've helped tens of thousands of people receive an autism diagnosis for the first time, work with neurodivergent-affirming therapists, and find belonging through community. Our outcomes meaningfully outperform traditional care for autistic adults, with substantially greater improvements in mood, anxiety, and quality of life.

Prosper is growing 3x year over year and are at mid-double-digit millions in run-rate revenue, with thousands of active clients and 400+ clinicians. We're a high-ownership, mission-driven team, building something that has never existed for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

The Opportunity

We're hiring Licensed Mental Health Therapists (LCSW, LPC, LMHC) to provide therapy for autistic and neurodivergent adults via telehealth. You'll join a team dedicated to creating affirming, accessible mental health services for the neurodivergent community.

Our clinicians come from diverse backgrounds and career stages - whether you're passionate about neurodiversity advocacy, seeking flexibility and better work-life balance, or looking to add specialized experience to your existing practice, we offer roles to match your professional goals.

Why Therapists Choose Prosper:

  • Focus on what matters most: Provide exceptional client care while we manage administrative tasks, insurance billing, and client acquisition

  • No-show and late cancellation reimbursement: Receive 50% reimbursement for late cancellations and no-shows
  • Grow professionally: Access regular peer consultation, specialized training, and monthly case conferences
  • Neurodiversity-affirming environment: Work alongside clinicians who share your commitment to neurodiversity-affirming approaches
  • Connect with a supportive clinical community: Join weekly drop-ins and engage in a tight-knit clinical community that prevent isolation

We offer two distinct position types to accommodate different career needs and scheduling preferences

Scheduling Availability

  • Set your own schedule, 7 days a week, between 7am and 10pm
  • No required evening, weekend or on-call hours
  • Build your schedule around your life, not the other way around

Full time (Benefits-Eligible)

  • Hours: Provide 25+ hours of weekly availability to build a caseload of 25+ clients
  • Ideal for: Those who seek steady, predictable income that grows with your client base
  • Compensation: Competitive hourly rate paid per session
  • Benefits: Comprehensive benefits package including Medical/Dental/Vision coverage, 401(k) retirement plan and PTO.

Part-Time Position

  • Hours: Provide 15+ hours of weekly availability to build a caseload of 15+ clients
  • Ideal For: Practitioners with existing commitments who want to diversify their practice or add specialized neurodiversity experience to your clinical portfolio
  • Compensation: Competitive hourly rate paid per session

Who We're Looking For:

Qualifications:

  • Licensed independent mental health professional (LCSW, LPC, LMHC)
  • Strong clinical skills in evidence-based modalities such as CBT, DBT or ACT
  • Interest in working with autistic or neurodivergent adults
  • Comfort with technology and virtual care platforms (Zoom, EHR, Slack)
  • Excellent communication skills and commitment to client-centered care
  • Telehealth experience preferred but not required

You'll Thrive Here If:

  • You identify with our mission to support the neurodivergent community
  • You're seeking better work-life balance without sacrificing meaningful clinical work
  • You're transitioning from a demanding in-person setting and want more flexibility
  • You want to maintain multiple practice settings and add specialized experience
  • You're passionate about providing affirming care to traditionally underserved populations

Compensation:

Our transparent model means your income grows with your client relationships. Unlike traditional salary models, our fee-for-service approach rewards you directly for the sessions you provide. The more sessions you complete, the more your practice thrives – with the security of guaranteed income during no-shows and cancellations. We pay between $X - $X per session.

Join Our Team

Ready to transform lives while advancing your career? Apply today to join Prosper Health's team of dedicated professionals making a real difference for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Prosper Health is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, including those who identify as neurodivergent, LGBTQ+, or BIPOC.

Competitive W2 rate paid per session. 50% reimbursement for late cancellations/no shows. Paid every 2 weeks for the sessions you provide, no waiting for payment or reimbursement. Benefit Eligible roles available that include Medical/Dental/Vision/401k/PTO

W2 Per Session Rate
$55—$60 USD

More about Prosper Health

  • Our culture is a unique mix of thoughtfulness, kindess, and high-performance. We set ambitious goals and hold ourselves accountable to achieving them.
  • We always ensure that we integrate perspectives from experts in our space, including clinicians and autistic self-advocates.
  • Our team members come from places such as Bain, McKinsey, BCG, FirstHand Health, Rula, SeatGeek, Benchling, and schools like Harvard, MIT, Stanford, Yale, Penn, Dartmouth, Northwestern, Vanderbilt, and more.

    • Find a Way - We use ingenuity, scrappiness, and determination to bend the world to accomplish our goals. We’re resourceful and do more with less.
    • Raise the Bar - We grow deliberately, by asking how things can improve and by giving and seeking feedback. We insist on the highest standards and keep pushing them higher.

The Opportunity

Euna Solutions is seeking a talented Senior AI Developer to be a key participant in our ambitious AI transformation of our finance platform for local and state government agencies. We are raising the bar on every part of the development process with an intentional agentic focus. This isn’t an idea, it’s accelerating taking what we have already achieved to the next level and it’s a great opportunity for an innovative curious AI developer who wants to push the boundaries and learn and work with some incredible talent.

The idea is to take this to the next level building applications with AI capabilities from the ground up. We need developers who know what good looks like, not just the code but all the other considerations necessary for building and designing enterprise grade software.

You'll own the hard problems: orchestration patterns that hold up under real-world load, developer experiences that let your teammates move fast with confidence, and engineering decisions that turn ambiguous requirements into concrete, operable systems.

What You'll Do:

Platform Ownership

  • Own the evolution of shared AI components, libraries, and platform capabilities the whole team builds on. You set the bar for reliability, testability, and developer experience — not as a reviewer, but as the person who ships it.

AI Feature Development

  • Design and build AI-powered product features end-to-end: LLM orchestration, prompt engineering workflows, evaluation, and observability. Carry work from requirements shaping through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.

Delivery Systems

  • Design and build the CI/CD patterns, deployment pipelines, observability tooling, and developer workflows that make shipping agents to production predictable and repeatable.

AI Tooling Leadership

  • Lead the team on AI tooling adoption — coding assistants, agentic development workflows, evaluation frameworks. Set the patterns that give teammates real leverage, not just access.

Backend Platform Engineering

  • Build and optimize the core SaaS platform systems AI features depend on: high-scale background processing, scalable APIs, ingestion pipelines, search and discovery, and PostgreSQL performance.

Technical Vision

  • Articulate a clear engineering direction to your team and to stakeholders. Translate ambiguous problems into concrete plans. Build shared understanding across engineering and product so everyone's rowing the same way.

Mentorship & Growth

  • Actively grow the engineers around you. Run technical reviews, establish best practices, and create an environment where the team can move quickly without constantly second-guessing their decisions.

What You Bring (as many as possible)

  • 7+ years of hands-on software development, with deep proficiency in at least one modern backend or full-stack language and breadth across the full SDLC
  • Understanding of agentic system design: orchestration, tool use, memory, retrieval, evaluation, and agent-to-agent communication — with the judgment to make the right architectural calls under real constraints
  • Some hands-on experience with production agentic tooling — orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI), LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock), vector databases, and evaluation/observability platforms (LangSmith, PromptLayer)

  • Deep grasp of SaaS architecture principles — you design systems others build on top of, and you understand the tradeoffs between speed, scalability, and maintainability at each layer
  • Proven track record building developer platforms and delivery systems — CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, testing frameworks, and the processes that let teams ship AI features rapidly and safely
  • Strong background in background processing systems (Redis-backed job queues, schedulers) and high-scale data pipelines
  • Solid understanding of PostgreSQL schema design and performance optimization
  • Experience designing and operating production REST APIs (auth, versioning, validation)
  • Understanding in Event Driven Development.
  • Experience with search and discovery systems (full-text, semantic, or vector search)
  • Strong understanding of security best practices (auth, data isolation, secrets management)
  • A demonstrated AI-first development approach — concrete examples of using LLMs and agentic tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) across the full breadth of daily engineering work, not just AI features

Nice to Have

  • Experience in government tech, public sector, or another compliance-heavy domain (auditability, data isolation, security reviews)

Who are we and why should you join us?

BetterHelp is on a mission to remove the traditional barriers to therapy and make mental health care more accessible to everyone. Founded in 2013, we are now the world’s largest online therapy service, providing affordable and convenient therapy across the globe. Our network of over 30,000 licensed therapists has helped millions of people take ownership of their mental health and change their lives forever. And we’re not stopping there – as the unmet need for mental health services continues to grow, BetterHelp is committed to being part of the solution.

As the Senior Manager, Enterprise Sales at BetterHelp, you’ll join a diverse team of licensed clinicians, engineers, product pros, creatives, marketers, and business leaders who share a passion for expanding access to therapy. And as a mental health company, we take employee mental health just as seriously as we do our mission. We deeply invest in our team’s well-being and professional development, because we know that business and individual growth go hand-in-hand. At BetterHelp, you’ll carve your own path, make an immediate impact, and be challenged every day – with a supportive community behind you the whole way.

What are we looking for?

BetterHelp is looking for aSenior Manager, Enterprise Sales with experience and passion for prospecting new clients, building meaningful relationships, and closing new business.

This is a senior individual contributor role with ownership of a defined SMB and Mid-Market territory and the full new-business sales cycle, from building pipeline and opening new doors to developing opportunities, navigating key stakeholders, negotiating, and closing new business.

The ideal candidate knows how to build a business, not simply manage a pipeline. You’re comfortable creating opportunities from the ground up, developing trusted relationships with employers, brokers, consultants, and other partners, and adapting your approach across both fast-moving SMB deals and more complex Mid-Market opportunities. You bring strong commercial judgment, curiosity, accountability, and an entrepreneurial mindset to your work.

What will you do?

  • Own and consistently deliver against an individual new-business bookings quota across an assigned SMB and Mid-Market territory.
  • Develop and execute a territory strategy that identifies priority accounts, market opportunities, key relationships, and the most effective paths to growth.
  • Build and maintain a healthy pipeline through outbound prospecting, inbound opportunities, broker and consultant relationships, partnerships, events, referrals, and other channels.
  • Partner with a variety of clients such as employers, non-profits, universities, government agencies, and both local and multinational organizations.
  • Own opportunities from initial engagement and discovery through negotiation, contracting, and signed agreement.
  • Lead thoughtful discovery conversations to understand prospective clients’ business needs, workforce challenges, decision criteria, and buying processes.
  • Deliver compelling presentations, business cases, and proposals that clearly connect BetterHelp’s solutions to each prospective client’s needs.
  • Navigate multiple decision-makers and influencers across opportunities of varying size and complexity.
  • Lead pricing discussions, contract negotiations, RFPs, and other critical stages of the sales process within established commercial parameters.
  • Build deep and meaningful relationships with employers, brokers, consultants, and other partners across the HR and Benefits ecosystem.
  • Maintain strong ownership of pipeline health, opportunity progression, CRM accuracy, KPI performance, and forecast reliability.
  • Use sales data, market intelligence, competitive insights, and pipeline trends to continuously evaluate and strengthen your territory and sales strategy.
  • Gain meaningful insight into client needs and work cross-functionally with Sales Leadership, Partnerships, Consultant Relations, Marketing, Product, Clinical, Operations, and other teams to develop the right solutions and advance opportunities.
  • Bring forward prospective client feedback, competitive intelligence, and market trends to help strengthen BetterHelp’s Enterprise sales approach.
  • Share successful approaches and lessons learned with the broader team as we continue to build and evolve our Enterprise business.
  • Have complete ownership of your opportunities and provide a thoughtful, responsive, and high-quality experience for prospective clients throughout the sales process.

What will you NOT do?

  • You will NOT worry about "runway", "cash left", or "how much time we have until the next round". We have the startup DNA but we're fully backed and funded, all the way to success.
  • You will NOT be confined to your "job". You will get involved in product, marketing, business strategy, and almost everything we do.
  • You will NOT be bogged down by office politics, ego, or bad attitude. Only positive, pleasure-to-work-with people are allowed here!
  • You will NOT get yourself burned out. We work hard but we believe in maintaining a sustainable work/life balance. Really.

Can I work remotely?

Yes. We operate on PST and candidates in any time zone are welcome to apply. We ask employees to travel to our San Jose, CA office up to three times per year plus one company-wide offsite to collaborate in person and strengthen working relationships. Travel expenses are covered and reasonable accommodations are made for those under unique circumstances who cannot travel.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 8+ years of B2B sales experience, including experience owning new-business sales cycles and revenue targets within SMB and/or Mid-Market segments.
  • Demonstrated experience in Direct-to-Employer (D2E) sales and/or the HR and Benefits market.
  • A demonstrated track record of meeting or exceeding individual new-business bookings or revenue targets.
  • Experience developing meaningful relationships with brokers, consultants, channel partners, and/or employer decision-makers.
  • Strong prospecting and business development skills with the ability to create opportunities from the ground up.
  • Previous experience leading complex sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders, pricing discussions, negotiations, contracts, and/or RFPs.
  • Strong commercial judgment and the ability to independently prioritize accounts and opportunities based on business potential and likelihood to close.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, from your email inbox habits and time management to keeping your CRM and pipeline up to date.
  • Entrepreneurial with an ability to create and follow plans while remaining flexible enough to respond to change and balance multiple opportunities and priorities.
  • Strong and efficient communicator, both written and verbal.
  • Ability to work independently while building strong relationships and collaborating effectively across teams.
  • Genuine curiosity about prospective clients and a relationship-driven approach to selling.
  • Passionate about the intersection of technology, healthcare, and expanding access to mental health support.

Benefits

  • Remote work with regular in-person bonding experiences sponsored by the company
  • Competitive compensation
  • Holistic perks program (including free therapy, employee wellness, and more)
  • Excellent health, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401k benefits with employer matching contribution
  • The chance to build something that changes lives – and that people love
  • Any piece of hardware or software that will make you happy and productive
  • An awesome community of co-workers

  • Experience with one or more SDK development languages and environments, such as TypeScript/JavaScript for web, Kotlin/Java for Android, or Swift/Objective-C for iOS, with the ability to understand implementation constraints and collaborate effectively with SDK engineering teams.
  • Scripting ability, preferably in Python, for building research tools, automation, and analysis workflows.
  • Ability to work independently on ambiguous problems and communicate findings clearly to engineering, product, and research stakeholders.

Advantages

  • Experience with Web SDKs, Mobile SDKs, client-side telemetry, device intelligence, behavioral signals, AI agent detection, or fraud detection products.
  • Experience researching bots, credential stuffing, scraping, headless browsers, AI-assisted automation, app cloning, SDK abuse, phishing kits, malware, or
  • anti-detection frameworks.
  • Experience with reverse engineering Android or iOS applications.
  • Familiarity with detection quality measurement, feature evaluation, false-positive analysis, production monitoring, or machine learning concepts.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or a related field— or equivalent hands-on experience.

Your day-to-day in this position

  • Research browser, WebView, Android, and iOS environments from an attacker’s perspective.
  • Identify new security signals, behavioral indicators, and technical patterns that can improve fraud, abuse, automation, and AI agent detection.

  • anti-detection methods.

jobs.description:
Stacklok is led by CEO Craig McLuckie and CTO Joe Beda, two of the creators of Kubernetes. As AI reshapes how software is built and used, we're building the foundation enterprises need to adopt it with confidence.

We're building the control plane for enterprise AI agents, enabling organizations to run, govern, and secure them on the infrastructure they already trust. Through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers running across Kubernetes and private cloud environments, AI agents can securely connect to internal data and systems while meeting the security, compliance, and operational requirements of highly regulated and security-conscious organizations. We've also extended this foundation to the model layer with an enterprise AI gateway.

The Stacklok Enterprise Platform is built on ToolHive, our open source MCP platform, and is already being adopted by leading technology companies and organizations in regulated industries. We also help maintain the official MCP registry and contribute openly to the community shaping the future of enterprise AI.

Location

This is a remote role based in Singapore. Candidates must live and work in Singapore and be legally authorized to work in Singapore.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at Stacklok, you sit where platform engineering meets AI, bringing deep Kubernetes expertise to help enterprises adopt Stacklok Enterprise and run AI agents securely on the infrastructure they already trust. Every environment is different, so the role builds the custom operators that fit the platform to each customer's stack and reach production fast.

This is hands-on, high-ownership work, and it is not only technical. Forward-deployed engagements run end to end through the role: standing up custom proof-of-concepts for Design Partners and customers, extending the platforn, coordinating the technical work, and keeping customer and team aligned as things move toward production. When unlocking value means changing how the product deploys to Kubernetes, that work comes back to the platform itself.

Kubernetes expertise is what unlocks value fast, and demand for this work is outpacing our capacity. The role offers a front-row seat to how leading enterprises put AI into production, and real influence over what gets built next. For a platform engineer who wants that expertise to land directly with customers, this is the chance to do it at the frontier of enterprise AI.

What Success Looks Like: First 6-12 Months

  • Ramped quickly on the platform and Stacklok Enterprise architecture, becoming the technical SME the AppliedAI team relies on for enterprise engagements.
  • Built trusted relationships across the team and with customers, and resolved a real customer blocker or shipped a first meaningful change.
  • Took one or more Design Partners from proof-of-concept to a working production deployment of Stacklok's Enterprise platform.
  • Unblocked enterprise adoption by improving how the product deploys to Kubernetes, measurably cutting time-to-value for customers.
  • Turned field learnings into a reusable engagement playbook and tooling, using AI-assisted workflows to make the next deployment faster for the whole team.

In This Role, You Will

  • Drive forward-deployed engagements end to end, from scoping each customer's technical goals and designing the deployment approach to taking POCs to a working state and toward production.
  • Design and deliver changes to the platform and to how it deploys to Kubernetes, unblocking enterprise adoption and contributing those changes back to Stackok Enterprise.
  • Act as the technical SME for enterprise adoption, answering deep platform and Kubernetes questions and giving hands-on support to customers and Design Partners.
  • Own the technical calls within your domain, moving quickly on reversible decisions and pulling in the team anchor as scope and risk grow.
  • Partner with senior peers and bring field insight back through standup, planning, and design reviews to influence priorities and how engagements run.
  • Coach teammates in your areas of deep expertise, especially Kubernetes, and contribute to hiring when needed.
  • Apply AI-assisted workflows and strengthen reusable tooling and playbooks so each engagement moves faster for the team.

Desired Skill & Experience

We do not expect every candidate to meet every point below. If this role excites you and you bring most of it, we encourage you to apply.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: writes well-structured production code with sound design and testing judgment.
    |
  • Deep Kubernetes expertise across cluster architecture, workload types, networking, storage, RBAC, and resource management, with Helm authoring and GitOps via Flux or ArgoCD across managed Kubernetes.
  • Strong operator and CRD literacy: reasons about control loops, CRD versioning, status, and finalizers, and writes controllers in Go using Kubebuilder or the Operator SDK.
  • Solid grasp of observability across metrics, logs, and traces, and when each applies. Familiarity with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, and platforms like Datadog or Grafana is a plus.
  • Comfortable working directly with customers, including over-the-shoulder debugging across varied enterprise permission models, and clearly communicating root causes and remediation steps.
  • A track record of delivering production-grade systems, mentoring engineers, and contributing fixes upstream to the underlying platforms and tools. Hands-on experience with MCP servers or AI agent tooling is a strong plus.
  • AI-first mindset: an active user of AI coding assistants who brings agentic workflows (skills, agents, rules, hooks) into daily work and experiments with AI to automate and accelerate delivery.
  • Communication: excellent written and verbal communication, able to explain complex technical ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Startup mentality and intrinsic motivation: self-directed and hands-on, thrives in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, and drives clarity through action.

Why Join Us?

At Stacklok, we believe great technology is built by teams that support, challenge, and inspire one another. We are AI maximalists, confident in its potential and committed to ensuring it is used in ways that are safe and sustainable.

You will join a highly motivated, collaborative team with deep experience building some of the world's most impactful technologies, with strong roots in open source, cloud-native technologies, security, and developer tools.

We offer competitive compensation and equity, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible PTO and paid holidays, paid parental leave, and a flexible, hybrid-or-remote work environment, plus team offsites in unique destinations to collaborate and connect in person.

If you're excited about the future of AI and want to build alongside people who care deeply about their craft, their community, and each other, we would love to hear from you.

We are changing FINANCE to finance CHANGE!

At Climate First Bank, we’re redefining what banking can be. As a Florida Benefit Corporation and FDIC-insured commercial bank, we offer a full suite of personal and business services—including solar, residential, commercial, ESOP Banking, Structured Finance and SBA loans—all designed to power a better future. We’re proud to be a Certified B Corporation, a member of 1% for the Planet, and part of the Global Alliance for Banking on Values (GABV), reflecting our deep commitment to sustainability, transparency, and ethical banking.

Join the Movement

We’re seeking driven, mission-aligned individuals ready to make an impact. If you’re passionate about sustainability, thrive in a fast-paced, results driven environment, and want to be part of something bigger, you will feel right at home.

Please note that benefit eligibility varies by employment status and that benefits for part-time employees may differ from those listed below.

What to expect as a Business Development Officer (BDO)

The Business Development Officer (BDO) for Factoring and Asset-Based Lending (ABL) is responsible for originating, structuring, and closing new business opportunities. This role is integral to the growth and success of the Structured Finance Division, requiring a proactive approach to business development, client relationship management, and industry engagement.

What You’ll Contribute in This Role:

Business Development

  • Identify, cultivate, and manage relationships with prospective clients.
  • Develop and execute a strategy to meet or exceed annual new business funding targets.
  • Leverage industry networks, referral sources, and marketing strategies to generate a consistent pipeline of high-quality leads.

Sales & Client Management

  • Conduct in-depth needs assessments to understand client financial requirements and present tailored financing solutions.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with referral partners, including brokers, CPAs, attorneys, and industry associations.

Structuring & Closing Deals

Market & Industry Expertise

Entrepreneurial Self-Starter Mentality - You take charge of your work product and take pride in delivering consistently great and measurable results. Job Summary

At Fuze Health, we put patients first and tirelessly address the most pressing needs in healthcare. We empower millions to digitally connect with care providers, essential health resources and needed treatments – and enable care providers, employers, health plans and life sciences companies to meaningfully enhance quality, outcomes and value. We are dedicated to helping our partners evolve and modernize to meet emerging patient and marketplace needs.

Fuze Health’s foundation is built upon the strategic combination of several proven, technology-powered innovators in the digital health, diagnostics, and pharmacy sectors. Our growing portfolio brings together the capabilities of industry leaders including LetsGetChecked, Truepill, and Alto Pharmacy, to create a distinctive, unified force in healthcare. Together, we have the shared vision, advanced capabilities and talented teams to deliver next-generation solutions that patients and healthcare partners need today and into the future.



Job Description

The Senior Manager, Safety & Quality drives operational excellence and compliance across FuzeRx. Acting as the central operational quality leader, this role partners to transform complex regulatory guidelines into seamless, automated workflows that safeguard data integrity, quality, safety, and end-to-end patient experiences. You will fully own and continuously optimize the pharmacy’s Quality Management System (QMS), scaling robust standard operating procedures (SOPs), Corrective & Preventative Action (CAPA) management, and proactive audit readiness to support our fast-moving, outcomes-focused ecosystem. Partnering dynamically across our cross-functional operations, product, tech, enterprise support, and clinical teams, you will leverage real-time analytics and root-cause metrics to mitigate risk, build next-generation standards, and cultivate a proactive culture of continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities:

Quality Management

  • Own FuzeRx’s quality management systems (QMS), including for supply chain and manufacturing partners
  • Develop and maintain quality policies, SOPs and work instructions
  • Ensures recalls, deviations, CAPA, complaints, adverse events and investigations are documented, tracked and resolved in conjunction with regulatory team and appropriate leaders
  • Facilitate inspection and audit readiness in conjunction with compliance across operations
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen the quality culture
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to resolve quality issues and prevent recurrence

Quality Analytics & Reporting

  • ​Manage the compilation, accuracy, and timely submission of quality metrics to external bodies, including licensing boards, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and accreditation organizations (e.g. URAC)
  • Design, track, interpret and present comprehensive quality dashboards, error rates, and performance KPIs to senior leadership
  • Monitor and react to trends across medication errors, near misses, dispensing quality, patient complaints, shipping quality, and customer-specific quality metrics
  • Analyze data to identify recurring issues and emerging risks

Operations Excellence and Patient Experience

  • Conduct root cause analyses for quality events and operational failures
  • Partner with cross-functional leaders to initiate and implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).
  • Recommend and lead process improvements that reduce variation and improve quality and safety
  • Measure the effectiveness of implemented quality improvements
  • Analyze patient complaints and satisfaction trends, identify operational drivers impacting patient experience
  • Develop recommendations that improve service quality, turnaround times and patient outcomes and partner with Customer Experience teams to reduce repeat issues

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with compliance, operations, clinical services, enterprise and regulatory affairs teams
  • Provide guidance and training to internal stakeholders on quality best practices
  • Hire and develop team members, manage performance of the team
  • Provide direct oversight, strategic direction, and daily management to the quality team
  • Cultivate a robust culture of continuous learning by building clear career paths, providing regular mentorship, and conducting performance reviews and fostering development

Required Experience & Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Graduate of an accredited school of pharmacy and a Licensed Pharmacist (RPh) in good standing with a state Board of Pharmacy and any non-resident licenses as dictated by business strategy
  • 5+ years of management experience in quality, or compliance functions
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, or healthcare supply chain quality assurance
  • Strong knowledge of FDA, DEA, cGMP, and state pharmacy regulations
  • Experience conducting and managing CAPA and implementing QMS processes
  • Strong collaboration skills with the ability to partner across supply chain, operations, clinical, and regulatory teams
  • Proficiency in standard tools and systems such as GSuite, Slack, and digital quality management systems
  • Excellent organizational and communication skills, with proven ability to influence stakeholders and vendors

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven track record of managing, mentoring, and scaling a technical or clinical quality team
  • Experience in a fast-paced, start-up environment; a self-starter, who takes initiative, ownership and drives towards results
  • Strong ability to synthesize complex data into clear, concise internal and external communication and action
  • Formal process improvement training (Lean / Six Sigma)
  • Formal quality certification
  • Formal project management training / certification



Additional Information

Physical requirements for this role include the ability to work at a computer terminal with monitor, keyboard and mouse for extended periods of time, stoop, bend, and reach for equipment and supplies, make frequent repetitive motions required to operate a computer that include the wrists, hands and fingers, and lift, carry, push, pull, and move light objects up to 20 pounds. The role also requires the ability to effectively communicate through verbal interactions, discern auditory information, and visually perceive details to perform essential job functions.

Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and similar applicable state laws, it is Fuze Health’s policy to provide reasonable accommodation to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship.

Salary and Benefits

Salary Range: $145,600-$182,000

Commission Eligible: No

Travel: No - Required up to 0% of the time

Location Requirement: Alto is limited to individuals residing in the following states: Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Florida, Kansas, Maryland, Missouri, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Washington (WA), and Wisconsin.

Employment Authorization Requirement: Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.

Benefits: Full-time employee benefits include: dental, vision, and multiple group medical plans to choose from, a 401(k) retirement savings plan, group life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, flexible spending account (FSA) and health savings account (HSA), commuter benefits, employer-paid short-term (STD) and long-term disability (LTD) insurance, and additional supplemental insurance plans (spouse life insurance, legal insurance, an employee assistance program, home health testing kits, and a fertility medication discount program). Employees are also provided flexible vacation time, accrued paid sick time, 10 paid holidays, (2 floating holidays for full time non-exempt employees) , and eight weeks of paid parental leave for eligible employees, additional paid weeks for the birthing parent, 4 weeks paid caregiver leave, and a Lifestyle Spending Account allowance each month.

More Benefits Information Here: Fuze Health Benefits Site.

Application deadline: October 1, 2026

Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis. If you have a disability and require reasonable accommodation during any portion of the application or hiring process, please contact us at .

About the Role

Outsource Ability is recruiting on behalf of a UK short-term rental operator for a highly organised Executive Assistant / Operations Manager to support the running of a serviced accommodation portfolio and the day-to-day work of the business owner.

The purpose of the role is to oversee the smooth running of the business. You will hold the team accountable for agreed tasks, keep property operations running to standard, manage property bills and administration, and provide direct personal and business support so that operational work does not fall back on the owner. After an initial handover, you will be expected to work largely independently.

Key Responsibilities

Team & Task Management
