jobs.description:
Hi, I'm Manu, Engineering Manager at Customer.io. We're looking for experienced backend engineers who want to build and own the infrastructure that powers one of the most data-intensive platforms in marketing automation — systems that process millions of events per second, orchestrate complex workflows at scale, and keep everything running reliably for thousands of customers worldwide.

You'll work on the Platform team, tackling hard distributed systems problems: designing for fault tolerance, scaling services under real production pressure, and building the foundational layers that every other team at Customer.io depends on. This isn't just maintenance work — you'll shape the architecture of systems that need to be both highly available and constantly evolving.

If you're someone who gets energized by the intersection of scale, reliability, and developer experience — and wants ownership over infrastructure that truly matters — we'd love to talk.

What you'll bring:

  • Deep experience with distributed systems and large-scale backend architecture
  • Strong instincts around reliability, observability, and fault tolerance
  • Comfort reasoning about performance, capacity, and trade-offs at scale
  • Experience with event-driven systems, message queues, or data pipelines is a plus
  • A collaborative mindset — you raise the team around you

About Customer.io

Over 9,000 companies - from scrappy startups to global brands - use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive.

We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data. Under the hood: Go, React, Ember and AI help us ship fast and scale with confidence.

Ownership

You drive technical direction across systems and teams. You move with urgency, build with empathy, and think long-term. You’ve led large-scale infrastructure initiatives and know what it takes to get them over the line.

Engineers with customer focus

You think about how infrastructure unlocks customer value. You care about developer experience, system design, and how your work shapes the customer experience.

A healthy disregard for “the way things are done”

You bring rigor and creativity. Best practices matter, but never more than forward motion.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and evolve distributed systems in Go to handle billions of daily events and messages and store and index petabytes of data
  • Lead architectural decisions around performance, reliability, and real-time event processing
  • Improve service-to-service communication through better APIs, messaging systems, and event-driven patterns
  • Work across teams to uncover bottlenecks and system issues, and lead initiatives to resolve them for a smoother customer experience
  • Tackle high-throughput challenges across data pipelines, queues, and scheduling infrastructure
  • Able to debug production systems at scale using effective instrumentation, and resolve issues quickly and confidently
  • Share knowledge and raise the bar through sharing your progress publicly with short videos, thoughtful writing, and mentorship
  • Leverage AI tools to prototype, move faster, and make better decisions

What we're looking for

  • Significant experience (typically 10+ years) building scalable, distributed systems in Go (or similar statically typed languages)

  • Comfort working in cloud-native environments (AWS, GCP)
  • Familiarity with APIs, observability, and operating production systems
  • A bias for action over perfection, and pride in owning technical decisions

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role is $150,000 - $200,000 USD (or equivalent in local currency) depending on experience and subject to market rate adjustment.

We know our people are what make us great, and we’re committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family. We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO, stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.

See full benefits here →

Our Process

No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.

  • Application - We review everyone with care. Tell us why you're interested.
  • Recruiter Call (30 mins) - Let’s chat about what you’re looking for and how we work.
  • Behavioral Interview (60 mins) - Talk with one of our hiring managers. We’ll explore topics like ownership, product thinking, and collaboration.
  • System Design Interview (60 mins) - A collaborative system design conversation focused on scaling challenges.

All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process.

Customer.io recognizes the stifling impact of systemic injustice on diverse communities. We commit to using our influence to increase inclusion and equity within the tech industry. We strive to build an inclusive team culture, implement bias-free hiring practices, and develop community partnerships to expand our global impact.

Zoom is the only video conference platform that we use, virtual interviews will be conducted using the video capability (i.e., not via the chat), and offers will be extended in writing on official Customer.io letterhead. Please be vigilant in all of your job search activity, and if you have any questions please contact .

Join us!

The architect defines system solutions based on user/client needs, cost, and required integration with existing applications, systems, or platforms. This employee also researches, identifies, selects, and tests technology products required for solution delivery. Establishes, implements, and documents technology integration or migration strategies. The employee must have the ability to proactively identify needs within the organization and, using expert technical and industry knowledge, design and build new solutions in support of organizational goals.


Core Responsibilities:

  • Engineers new workflows or optimize existing business processes that supersede existing standards set in place internally or by vendors utilizing expert knowledge crossing multiple clinical applications and operational areas.
  • Leads projects associated with application implementation and execution of high complexity and larger impact. Applies project management methodology and utilizes standard project management for software in development and maintenance of project plans.
  • Functions as an independent project lead or provides oversight for project manager and/or business analyst on assigned projects and recognize/ minimize business value lost during project/program execution.
  • Performs proactive analysis on current systems and technology in order to recommend potential changes or enhancements that will assist in adhering to organization's strategic vision and improve operational workflows as well as patient and end user experience.
  • Identifies product and customization requirements to effectively address necessary product configuration, while working within project scope and time line.
  • Serves as mentor to senior analysts and is proficient and/or certified in numerous applications.
  • Holds a comprehensive working knowledge and understands healthcare operational processes and job functions pertaining to assigned UHealth IT clinical applications and solutions.
  • Possesses expert knowledge of third party partnerships, experience with managing vendor relationships, and contract negotiations.
  • Provides support to the team in analyzing, resolving, and escalating complex integration problems encountered by the team during system implementations and upgrades.
  • Implement projects that are ahead of industry/peer trends. Thinks out of the box and follows the marking curve to stay on the forefront of Healthcare technology. Designs new solutions.
  • Participates in new hire orientation by providing the clinical application support in the work area required for the job role.
  • Collaborates with clinic leadership to develop or improve operational processes, polices, and procedures.
  • Participates in all clinical operations meetings to assess user feedback, gather future requirements for modifications, and provide a status on competency, adoption, and utilization rates.
  • Facilitates knowledge transfer of the technology-enabled user workflows and best practice use of applications.

At Jobscan, we’re passionate about empowering job seekers to land more interviews with AI. We have helped millions of job seekers get more interviews in 100+ countries. Jobscan’s platform benefits job seekers, employers, universities, and communities. We're a fast-growing startup 🚀. Since its founding in 2014, Jobscan has thrived for 11 years as a 100% self-funded company, achieving consistent profitability and rapid growth without VC investment. Recently, we’ve transformed into an AI-first company, leveraging cutting-edge tools to enhance operations and our product. This independence allows us to stay laser-focused on our customers, delivering impactful solutions for job seekers. Join us if you wish to be a part of a company that makes a real difference in people’s lives ❤️!

Summary

Jobscan is building a premium B2B business serving outcome-driven institutions that care deeply about employment results. This is not a volume-driven, script-following BDR role.
As a Business Development Representative, your job is not to convince everyone to take a meeting. Your job is to identify which institutions are genuinely aligned with how Jobscan creates value, and to qualify hard, challenge assumptions, and walk away when there isn’t a fit.
You’ll engage complex organizations (primarily universities and professional education programs), navigate multi-stakeholder buying dynamics, and represent a clear point of view about what actually drives student employment outcomes.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys thinking, learning, and having real conversations, especially when those conversations involve change.
Note: We receive a high volume of applications. Candidates who take the extra step to identify the hiring manager and send a brief, thoughtful note explaining why this role is a strong fit tend to stand out. If you are able to find a phone number, a concise and professional call is even better. This is a good proxy for how the role works in practice.

What you'll be doing:

  • Research target institutions, programs, and stakeholders to understand organizational structure, incentives, and buying dynamics before outreach
  • Initiate outbound conversations via phone, email, LinkedIn, and other channels to engage the right stakeholders
  • Lead early conversations that diagnose institutional readiness, outcome alignment, and fit - not just interest
  • Develop, test, and refine messaging tailored to different buyer personas (career services, program leadership, senior administrators)
  • Challenge prospects respectfully when their current approach is unlikely to drive real employment outcomes
  • Disqualify misaligned prospects confidently and professionally
  • Maintain and nurture a focused book of prospects with thoughtful follow-up and relevant insights
  • Run structured outreach experiments across messaging, channels, and timing; analyze results and apply learnings
  • Maintain clean, accurate records in the CRM to support prioritization, follow-up, and learning
  • Collaborate closely with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to share market feedback and improve how we engage the market
  • Stay informed on trends in hiring, higher education, and AI to engage prospects with credible, relevant insight

Required qualifications & experience:

    We are looking for candidates who fit either of the following profile backgrounds:
  • Sales & Outreach Background: 1+ year of experience as a Business Development Representative (BDR).
  • Domain Expertise Background: 3+ years of experience within Higher Ed (EDU).
    Direct sales experience is not required for candidates coming from this background.

What will help you succeed here:

  • Ability to articulate value clearly and comfortably initiate conversations with senior educational stakeholders.
  • Experience selling or marketing a B2B product/service (SaaS welcome) OR deep operational understanding of how educational institutions make purchasing decisions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate a point of view clearly and professionally.
  • Demonstrated business judgment and curiosity to understand how complex institutions operate and how to best advise them.
  • Comfort challenging assumptions and engaging in respectful disagreement when needed.
  • Ability to think critically about fit, readiness, and priority—focusing on relationship quality and strategic fit, not just raw activity volume.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and adapting your approach based on market feedback.
  • Familiarity with using a CRM (HubSpot or similar) to plan work, track relationships, and drive follow-up.
  • Strong analytical instincts to assess what messaging or targeting is working and make adjustments accordingly.
  • Experience leveraging AI tools for research, writing, or workflow optimization, with an interest in emerging tech within hiring and education.
  • High personal accountability and ownership over outcomes, not just activity.

We’d love it if you also brought:

  • Experience selling SaaS or subscription-based B2B products
  • Experience selling into higher education, government, or other committee-driven or regulated environments
  • Experience working at an early-stage company or on a lean team
  • Experience running structured outbound experiments and applying learnings to improve performance
  • Familiarity with sales fundamentals such as pipeline math, conversion rates, and opportunity qualification
  • Experience selling a differentiated or premium product where not every prospect was a fit

jobs.description:
Senior Director of Partnerships & Advocacy

National Programs Team

Location: Remote, or Hybrid if within 30 miles of Providence, RI

Position Type: Exempt, Full-time

Travel Requirements: 20% Travel

Start Date: ASAP

Reports to: Vice President, National Programs and External Affairs

ROLE OVERVIEW

Democrats for Education Reform (DFER) and its partner organizations, Education Reform Now (ERN) and Education Reform Now Advocacy (ERNA), are seeking an experienced and strategic Senior Director of Partnerships and Advocacy to lead high-impact national and state-level initiatives that advance educational opportunity for families across the country—especially low-income families and families of color.

This is a leadership role designed to grow over time. The Senior Director of Partnerships & Advocacy will initially focus with urgency and full investment on the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC)—a transformative and time-sensitive opportunity to expand available education dollars for families in states across the country. With 36 states holding gubernatorial elections in 2026, the window to build political will and secure FSTC opt-in commitments is immediate and consequential. Success in this phase will require rapid coalition building, deep government relations work, and sophisticated multi-state execution.

As the FSTC initiative matures, this role will evolve to lead other major organizational priorities adjacent to continued FSTC advocacy. These may include initiatives relevant to the 2028 presidential election cycle, emerging federal and state education policy opportunities, and other strategic initiatives where we seek to shape the national education landscape. The Senior Director of Partnerships & Advocacy will help define and build the organizational infrastructure for these future initiatives while executing on immediate priorities.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work for any employer in the United States and will be required to submit proof of eligibility. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

WHO WE ARE

Democrats for Education Reform (DFER) is a national political organization that supports elected Democrats and candidates for office who seek to expand policies and practices that work well for America’s students and confront those that do not. We are education advocates who prioritize students and families, especially low-income students and students of color who should be better served by our country’s education system.

Education Reform Now Advocacy (ERNA) is an advocacy group that advances education reform measures through executive and legislative engagement strategies and political advocacy work. ERNA keeps constant pressure on elected officials to champion policy that drives progress towards a high-quality public education system for low-income students and students of color.

Education Reform Now (ERN) is a nonpartisan think tank that promotes increased resources and innovative reforms in K–12 public education, particularly for students of color and students from low-income families.

WHAT WE DO

1. Support for Forward-Thinking Education Leaders — In an approach that is markedly different from our peers and partners in the field, DFER engages directly with candidates and elected officials to empower them to advocate for education policies that focus foremost on serving students. Our partner organization, Education Reform Now, does work that involves policy research, analysis and education that helps policy makers at all levels understand complex education issues and make informed decisions.

2. Informing the Education Debate — Our coalition work reflects the breadth of our policy priorities. We work collaboratively with organizations and our community networks to create an education system that serves and is held accountable to all students and families.

3. Targeted Interventions and Rapid Response — DFER’s reach, from the most local district relationships to state and federal policymakers, enables us to respond quickly to the changing landscape and policy trends. Activities vary significantly from project to project and may include training, policy analysis, public engagement, electoral and issue advocacy, and policy guidance for elected officials and local advocates.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The responsibilities of the Senior Director of Partnerships and Advocacy will be shaped by the campaign cycle and organizational priorities at any given time. In the near term, they will center on FSTC; over time they will expand to encompass additional initiatives.

Immediate Focus: FSTC Initiative Leadership (2025–2026)

The FSTC represents an urgent and time-limited opportunity. The Senior Director of Partnerships and Advocacy will be expected to move quickly and execute with precision on the following:

  • Design and lead a comprehensive national and state strategy to build stakeholder support for FSTC opt-in across priority states, with an eye toward the 2026 gubernatorial election cycle.
  • Develop and manage state-specific plans, working closely with in-state coalition partners and policymakers.
  • Track gubernatorial and legislative developments in target states and adapt strategy in real time.
  • Synthesize data and research provided by our policy team and partner organizations to develop state-specific messaging and advocacy materials, such as factsheets, webinar presentations and toolkits.
  • Direct targeted multi-channel digital communications campaigns in 4–5 high-priority states to illustrate FSTC’s benefits for families.
  • Present results of polling and public opinion research, including national polls and deep-dive state-level polling in target states.

Ongoing: Government Relations & Coalition Building

  • Cultivate and maintain high-level relationships with center-left governors, gubernatorial candidates, and their senior staff on both official and campaign sides.
  • Build and sustain a structured coalition of national and state partners—including school choice and charter advocates, youth-serving organizations, and community groups—to ensure alignment and amplify advocacy efforts.

Ongoing: Organizational & Budget Management

  • Oversee budgets across 3 entities, ensuring resources are allocated effectively across communications, lobbying, polling, research, and coalition activities.
  • Direct outside consultants and manage vendor relationships.
  • Report to senior leadership and contribute to organizational fundraising by demonstrating campaign impact.

Future: Expanded Initiative Scope

As the FSTC campaign reaches key milestones, the Director of Partnerships and Advocacy will take on additional portfolios. Anticipated areas of expansion include:

  • Supporting organizational engagement in the 2028 presidential election cycle, including stakeholder outreach and voter-facing education advocacy.
  • Identifying and launching new mission-aligned state and federal initiatives aligned.
  • Building out organizational infrastructure—systems, processes, and partnerships—to support a growing multi-initiative operation.

COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION

Democrats for Education Reform welcomes applications from all, and strongly encourages women, people of color, people with disabilities, immigrants, refugees, and LGBTQ people to apply for this position. We are committed to maximizing the diversity of our organization and recruiting a team that reflects the diversity of the students we serve.

Requirements

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and skills:

  • Education Policy Knowledge — Significant knowledge of school choice, charter schools, and K–12 education reform policy is preferred. A commitment to educational equity and expanding opportunity for underserved families is non-negotiable.
  • Political & Advocacy Expertise — Familiarity with political campaigns, government affairs, or advocacy, with a track record of winning complex legislative or executive-branch campaigns at the state or federal level.
  • Deep Understanding of the Center-Left — Strong personal relationships with center-left governors, gubernatorial staff, presidential campaign alumni, or other executive-branch decision-makers are strongly preferred.
  • Coalition Building — Demonstrated ability to build and manage complex, multi-stakeholder coalitions across diverse political and community partners.
  • Strategic Communications — Ability to translate complex policy concepts into compelling narratives for policymakers, press, and the public; experience overseeing digital campaigns and earned media efforts.
  • Project & Budget Management — Experience managing multi-faceted campaigns with multiple workstreams, contractors, and budgets simultaneously.
  • Entrepreneurial Drive — Comfort operating in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment; ability to build systems and structures while executing on an ambitious timeline.
  • Long-Term Strategic Vision — Ability to think beyond the immediate campaign cycle and contribute to building organizational capacity for future priorities, including the 2028 presidential cycle.

Benefits

COMPENSATION

The compensation band for this role is $160,000 - $180,000. Compensation is competitive and commensurate with experience. DFER is proud to offer excellent benefits: health, vision, and dental coverage; cell phone and internet reimbursement; flexible spending plan; life insurance; short- and long-term disability insurance; 401K plan with a match; paid family leave; and paid time off (vacation, sick time, floating holidays, and all national holidays).

jobs.description:
Description

The Problem SE Solves

Enterprise buyers of AI/cyber need technical proof and trust. An Account Executive can build relationships and align on business value, but the moment a prospect's security architect or CISO asks "how does this actually work in our environment, and can you prove it won't create risk," a generalist AE either stalls the deal or gives an answer that erodes trust.

The Sales Engineer exists to remove that stall point: to be credible enough technically that skeptical buyers trust the answer, and fast enough to turn that trust into a scoped, winnable evaluation (POC) rather than an open-ended technical rabbit hole that kills momentum.

Put simply: AEs sell the vision, SEs prove it's real - and in security specifically, "prove it's real" often means proving it's safe, which is a much higher bar than a typical SaaS demo.

Key Goals

  1. De-risk technical objections before they stall a deal. Get ahead of architecture, security, and data-handling questions rather than reacting to them.
  2. Convert technical interest into a scoped, winnable evaluation. No vagueness. The SE's job is to define success criteria tight enough that a win is unambiguous.
  3. Shorten the technical evaluation cycle. Time-to-technical-validation is often the single biggest lever on overall sales cycle length in security deals.
  4. Build durable trust with technical buyers, independent of the AE relationship, technical buyers often remember and vouch for the SE specifically, which shows up in renewals/expansion later.
  5. Be the technical truth serum internally within Sola. flag deals that shouldn't be won (e.g., the product genuinely doesn't fit the use case) rather than overselling to hit quarter numbers.

About the Role

We're hiring a Sales Engineer to be the technical backbone of our sales process. You'll partner with Account Executives to run technical discovery, deliver compelling demos, lead proofs of concept (POCs), and answer the hard security and architecture questions prospects may ask.

This role is highly customer-facing and directly influences whether deals close.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with Account Executives throughout the sales cycle: discovery, technical evaluation, POC, and close
  • Run tailored product demos that map directly to a prospect's environment, threat model, and use cases
  • Design, scope, and run proofs of concept - defining success criteria with the customer and making sure we hit them
  • Answer technical, architecture, and security questions from prospects, including deep dives on deployment models, data handling, integrations, and model behavior
  • Respond to RFPs/RFIs and complete security questionnaires in partnership with Security and Legal
  • Build and maintain demo environments, sample datasets, and reusable POC assets
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor to prospects - not just presenting features, but helping them think through their own security architecture
  • Relay competitive intelligence, objections, and feature gaps back to Product and Marketing
  • Support technical onboarding handoff to the Forward Deployed / Customer Success team post-sale

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in a sales engineering, solutions engineering, or technical pre-sales role, ideally in cybersecurity, AI/ML, or enterprise infrastructure
  • Solid understanding of security fundamentals: Cloud Security, SecOps, SIEM/SOAR, EDR, network security, cloud security, or threat detection
  • Comfortable presenting to and fielding tough questions from technical buyers and executives (security architects, CISOs, engineering leads)
  • Hands-on technical ability: can read/write basic scripts (Python, Bash), understand APIs, and speak credibly about cloud architecture (AWS/GCP/Azure)
  • Strong communicator who can translate technical depth into business value, and vice versa
  • Experience scoping and running POCs with clear, mutually agreed success criteria
  • Comfortable with a fast-paced, quota-carrying-adjacent environment where your work directly affects revenue

Preffered

  • Experience selling or supporting AI/LLM-based products, and ability to speak credibly about model behavior, hallucination risk, and evaluation
  • Prior experience at a cybersecurity vendor (SIEM, EDR, XDR, SOAR, or similar)
  • Experience with demo environment tooling and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, etc.)

About Open

Open is building the category of AI-native customer communication.

For decades, companies have managed customer conversations through ticketing systems, helpdesks, call centers, and fragmented automation tools. These systems were built to help humans process customer requests.

We believe that era is ending.

The next generation of customer communication will be run by intelligent agents that can understand customers, reason across company knowledge and systems, take action, and communicate proactively, not just wait for customers to reach out.

Open is the platform for that new world.

Companies use Open to deploy autonomous AI agents across chat, email, WhatsApp, and voice, both inbound and outbound. These agents can resolve support requests, follow up with customers, recover missed opportunities, re-engage leads, trigger conversations at the right moment, and execute complex customer-facing workflows end to end.

Open does not just help companies respond faster. It gives them an intelligent communication layer that can decide when to engage, what to say, what action to take, and how to move the customer forward.

Over time, customer communication will stop being a collection of tickets and campaigns managed by separate systems. It will become one intelligent layer that continuously understands, acts, and communicates on behalf of the company.

Our ambition is to make Open the default infrastructure through which companies communicate with their customers.

Not another helpdesk.

The system of intelligence for customer communication.

We are backed by Y Combinator, SpaceTime, and Pioneer Fund.

The Role

Product Engineers at Open own problems end-to-end: from spotting an opportunity, to talking directly with users, to shipping the feature in production with no layers in between, no hand-off culture. You are a full-stack owner.

This role focuses on our telephony platform: phone numbers, SIP, call routing, and keeping enterprise voice traffic reliable at scale. You will work on a genuinely hard product, AI customer experience infrastructure used by enterprises at scale across Europe, the US, and the GCC. The codebase is React + TypeScript throughout. The problems are real, the users are live, and the impact is measurable and scalable.

If you want to work somewhere that trusts engineers to think, decide, and ship then look no further!

  • Identify product opportunities: Spot gaps or improvements before anyone asks you to. Bring proposals, not just execution.
  • Talk to users directly: Understand problems by speaking with the people experiencing them. No layers, no filtered requirements.
  • Ship features end-to-end: Plan, prioritise, and implement full-stack features (React + TypeScript) from concept to production.
  • Own quality: Code reviews, testing, performance, reliability this is your product as much as anyone's.
  • Collaborate closely: Work with the Customer Engineering team to incorporate real user feedback into what you build next.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • Experience with telephony or real-time communication systems (SIP, WebRTC, or similar) is a big plus.
  • 3+ years of experience building and shipping software products.
  • Strong TypeScript and React you are comfortable owning a full-stack feature without hand-holding.
  • Product instinct you can look at a workflow and know what to fix, not just implement what you are told.
  • Speed and quality in balance you ship fast without leaving messes.
  • Willingness to talk to customers and let reality shape your priorities.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Top-of-market compensation.
  • Full health insurance.
  • Equity participation we want you building this like you own it.
  • Direct collaboration with world-class engineers at a YC-backed company with real enterprise traction.

We are a small team. Every engineer here matters enormously. If you are the type who thrives with real ownership and real impact, Let’s talk.

Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

jobs.description:
ROLE SUMMARY


The NHS Solutions Partnerdevelops and delivers collaborative working projects with NHS organisations (e.g. Integrated Care Systems, Health Innovation Networks, Primary Care Networks, GP Federations, Hospital Trusts and the equivalents in the Devolved Nations), delivering value to the healthcare system, patients and Pfizer. The role builds trusted relationships with stakeholders, translates locally identified unmet need or service inefficiencies into well-governed partnership projects, and ensures every project is delivered, measured and disclosed in full compliance with the ABPI Code of Practice and relevant national guidance.


ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES


Opportunity identification and scoping

  • Position Pfizer as partner of choice in developing collaborative programmes with the NHS, offering solutions that address important issues and deliver meaningful impact.
  • Work with the cross-functional team and NHS stakeholders to identify service barriers, unmet need, or pathway inefficiencies where collaborative working could deliver a measurable improvement in patient care or system efficiency (e.g. diagnosis, treatment, resource utilisation, economic impact, patient experience/adherence).
  • Proactively consider with NHS partners how digital and AI solutions could support pathway transformation.
  • Define clear outcomes to be measured, the process for replication and scaling if outcomes are achieved, and the plan for long-term sustainability.

Project development and governance

  • Develop the Project Initiation Document (PID), defining objectives, scope, resource contributions from each partner, governance structure, outcome measures, timeline and exit strategy.
  • Lead the internal review process of the collaborative working project with medical, legal and compliance as required and identify an appropriate Executive Sponsor.
  • Draft and negotiate the Collaborative Working Agreement with the correct NHS legal entity (not with an individual), ensuring conflict-of-interest and dispute-resolution provisions are in place.
  • Arrange for certification of documents and publish a certified executive summary in advance of project initiation, in line with Code requirements.

Delivery and stakeholder management

  • Act as the project lead throughout project delivery, chairing or co-chairing the project board / governance group.
  • Coordinate internal contributions (health economics, medical affairs, data/RWE, digital/AI, project management) and any third-party delivery partners commissioned into the project.
  • Monitor progress against milestones and outcome measures; manage risks, variations and any dispute resolution required under the agreement and adjust accordingly.
  • Support the funded NHS role(s) or service change to transition toward sustainability, including input into any business case for continued local funding beyond the project end date.

Compliance, disclosure and reporting

  • Ensure all activity remains non-promotional and that it must not be, or be perceived to be, an inducement to prescribe, supply, recommend, buy or sell any medicine.
  • Ensure that where a collaborative project may increase the appropriate use of medicines in a pathway, including Pfizer medicines, that the pathway is in line with local NHS guidance and national guidance where it exists.
  • Maintain complete documentation of resource contributions, governance decisions and outcomes for audit purposes and ensure there is no access to individual patient data.
  • Ensure accurate transfer-of-value data for annual Disclosure UK reporting.
  • Publish a final outcomes report/summary at project close with measurement of agreed outcomes.

Measures of Success

  • Quality of collaborative working projects managed within the allocated budget available.
  • Achievement of patient care or system-efficiency outcomes against each project’s defined measures.
  • Successful transition of project-funded roles or service changes into sustainable local funding, where that is the intended outcome.
  • Scaling of successful projects to other areas (e.g. ICS wide, multiple ICSs, national).
  • Quality of relationships with NHS partners, evidenced through partner feedback and continued willingness to collaborate.
  • Nominations and winners of NHS partnership awards.
  • 100% compliance with internal review, disclosure and publication requirements across all live projects.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS


  • Significant experience in account management, healthcare partnerships or market access roles.
  • Strong understanding of NHS structures, commissioning, and funding flows in England and equivalent structures in Devolved Nations.
  • Excellent project management skills, including experience developing project initiation documents, business cases and outcome frameworks or similar.
  • Experience in pathway/service redesign and change management support.
  • Ability to build trusted, senior-level relationships with NHS executives and clinical leaders.
  • Sound commercial and analytical judgement.
  • Good working knowledge of the ABPI Code of Practice, especially in relation to Collaborative Working and Disclosure UK requirements.
  • Ability to translate local health system / NHS plan priorities into aligned, therapeutic-area solutions that overcome challenges and optimise patient care.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS


  • Experience in local data analysis and clinical audit support (building the case for change).
  • Experience in service evaluation measurement and health economics (demonstrating system benefits).
  • Experience supporting implementation of technology and AI solutions in the NHS to improve care pathways (patient identification, diagnosis/triage, remote monitoring, e-PROMS).
  • Experience managing multi-partner projects involving third-party delivery organisations (e.g. data/analytics or clinical staffing providers).

Person Specification

  • Acts with integrity.
  • Comfortable operating within a highly governed, audited environment, with strong attention to documentation and process.
  • Skilled at translating a clinical or operational problem into a structured, fundable project proposal.
  • Collaborative and consultative, able to influence without direct authority across both NHS and internal company stakeholders.
  • Resilient in managing projects that may run over 12-24 months, often against shifting NHS priorities and reorganisations.
  • Excellent communicator, strategic thinker, proactive leader and change agile.

Work location assignment: Remote (within UK)


Purpose

Breakthroughs that change patients' lives... At Pfizer we are a patient centric company, guided by our four values: courage, joy, equity and excellence. Our breakthrough culture lends itself to our dedication to transforming millions of lives.

Digital Transformation Strategy

One bold way we are achieving our purpose is through our company wide digital transformation strategy. We are leading the way in adopting new data, modelling and automated solutions to further digitize and accelerate drug discovery and development with the aim of enhancing health outcomes and the patient experience.

Flexibility

We aim to create a trusting, flexible workplace culture which encourages employees to achieve work life harmony, attracts talent and enables everyone to be their best working self. Let’s start the conversation!

Equal Employment Opportunity

We believe that a diverse and inclusive workforce is crucial to building a successful business. As an employer, Pfizer is committed to celebrating this, in all its forms – allowing for us to be as diverse as the patients and communities we serve. Together, we continue to build a culture that encourages, supports and empowers our employees.

DisAbility Confident

We are proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and we encourage you to put your best self forward with the knowledge and trust that we will make any reasonable adjustments necessary to support your application and future career. Our mission is unleashing the power of our people, especially those with unique superpowers. Your journey with Pfizer starts here!

To learn more about acceptable and prohibited uses of AI during the recruitment process, please review our candidate AI-use guidelines available on Pfizer Careers.

About the Role

Outsource Ability is recruiting on behalf of a UK serviced accommodation operator for an experienced Operations Manager to oversee guest experience, pricing and reputation across their property portfolio.

The core objective of the role is to keep the portfolio running to standard and well booked. You will oversee the standards of the guest communications team and handle escalated guest issues, manage pricing and availability across Airbnb and Booking.com, respond to companies enquiring about stays, and protect the business's reputation through active review management.

Key Responsibilities

Guest Communications & Team Oversight

  • Oversee the guest communications team and check that messages are answered promptly, accurately and in the agreed tone.
  • Review guest conversations regularly and give the team clear, constructive feedback.
  • Handle escalated guest issues and complaints personally, escalating to the client only where an issue falls outside your authority.
  • Cover guest messages when the team is short-staffed or volumes are high.
  • Maintain and improve message templates, saved replies and SOPs so that standards stay consistent.
  • Coordinate with cleaners, maintenance contractors and suppliers to fix property issues raised by guests.
  • Track the team's tasks through to completion and follow up directly where things slip.

Occupancy & Pricing

  • Adjust nightly rates, minimum stays and availability on Airbnb and Booking.com to keep properties booked at the right price.
  • Respond to changes in demand, seasonality and local events by updating pricing promptly.
  • Set up and manage promotions and discounts so that offers are structured correctly and do not stack beyond agreed limits.
  • Keep calendars, rates and restrictions accurate and in sync across all channels.
  • Flag properties with low occupancy early and suggest practical changes to improve bookings.

Inventory & Procurement

  • Track stock levels of linen, toiletries and consumables across all properties, working with cleaners to keep counts accurate.
  • Reorder supplies in good time so that properties are fully stocked before guests arrive.
  • Source and compare suppliers for recurring purchases and new property set-ups, within agreed budgets and spending limits.
  • Keep accurate records of purchases and property expenses.

Listings & Property Onboarding

  • Create and optimise listings, including titles, descriptions, photos and amenities, to improve visibility and conversion.
  • Coordinate new properties through to launch, including photography, staging and listing set-up, so that each property is ready to take bookings from day one.

Corporate & Direct Booking Enquiries

  • Handle enquiries from companies seeking accommodation, such as contractors, relocation agents and insurance claim handlers.
  • Explain the client's offer, agree terms within the authority given, and secure bookings and extensions.
  • Follow up on open enquiries promptly so that no opportunity is lost.
  • Build relationships with corporate clients to win repeat and longer-stay business.
  • Keep enquiry and booking records accurate, with statuses and next actions up to date.

Reputation & Reviews

  • Monitor and respond to reviews on Airbnb, Booking.com and Google promptly and professionally.
  • Encourage guests to leave reviews, using automated messaging where available.
  • Identify recurring issues in guest feedback and work with the team to resolve them.
  • Protect the review scores and platform ratings that affect listing ranking.

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • At least two years' experience in serviced accommodation, short-term rental or hospitality operations.
  • Hands-on experience managing listings, pricing and availability on Airbnb and Booking.com.
  • Experience handling guest communications and resolving complaints.
  • Experience overseeing a guest communications, customer service or similar team, including reviewing their work and giving feedback.
  • Confident communicating with businesses and negotiating bookings by telephone and email.
  • Experience managing online reviews and reputation.
  • Commercially minded and comfortable working with numbers and spreadsheets.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Able to work independently and judge what to handle and what to escalate.
  • Comfortable using AI tools and quick to learn new software.

Advantageous

  • Experience with dynamic pricing tools such as PriceLabs, Wheelhouse or Beyond.
  • Experience with a property management system or channel manager such as Guesty, Hostaway or Hospitable.
  • Experience with VRBO or other booking platforms.
  • Experience with corporate, contractor, relocation or insurance stays.
  • Experience managing inventory or purchasing across multiple properties.
  • Experience communicating with UK guests and businesses.
  • Experience creating or maintaining SOPs.

Remote Work Requirements

Applicants must:

  • Be based in South Africa.
  • Have a modern laptop or PC (Intel i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 or equivalent, minimum 8GB RAM).
  • Have a stable fibre connection with a minimum of 50 Mbps download and 50 Mbps upload.
  • Have a functional UPS, inverter or power station able to run a router and laptop for a minimum of 2–4 hours during load shedding.
  • Have a professional noise-cancelling headset with a clear microphone.
  • Have a quiet workspace suitable for calls and video meetings.
  • Be available for the agreed full-time hours during UK business times.

If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team.

Senior | Staff Product Engineer

Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) is hiring Senior and Staff Product Engineers to join our Technology team. In these hands-on, full-stack roles, you’ll work across our brand portfolio to design, build, and modernize our tech stack—from client-facing digital experiences to the internal operating system that runs our business.

We have openings at both levels and will align the title and scope to your experience.

You'll join a small, sharp team that solves real business problems with whatever works best, whether that's AI, custom code, or intelligently integrated enterprise systems. You'll write code, design solutions, and contribute to the culture we’re building at CHG.

Though early in adopting AI-driven development, we’re building an AI-first engineering team and want engineers who will help us get there. Day to day, that means paying attention to how we work, spotting technical gaps, and helping us iterate our way into the future. You'll help shape the tech and practices that we carry forward.

What You’ll Do:

  • Build end to end. Own features across the front end, back end, APIs, business logic, and data layer. You'll take them from ideation to production and beyond: measuring, learning, and continuously improving.
  • Connect the dots. A lot of the pieces are already there. Design how our systems fit together across brands, apps, and enterprise tools like Salesforce and NetSuite. Build the integrations that keep them talking, and handle client, employee, and financial data with security, privacy, and compliance in mind.
  • Turn problems into plans. Break ambiguous requirements into clear technical plans and reviewable units of work for humans and agents.
  • Work AI-native. Use AI agents across research, prototyping, implementation, testing, refactoring, and documentation, and verify what they produce.
  • Shape the foundation. Contribute to architecture, technology choices, and development patterns built to scale with the business.
  • Help set the standard. Introduce and refine AI development practices, tools, and workflows, and help teammates adopt them.
  • Wilderness coding. Leave it better than you found it. Make the codebase easier to work in, for people and agents alike. That means tests, monitoring, documentation, and architecture patterns that scale with the business.
  • Collaborate. Partner with product, design partners, and engineering to clarify requirements and explain trade-offs. Participate in code review, pairing, onboarding, and mentorship.

What We Look For:

  • You have 6+ years of experience engineering production software for Senior level, or 9+ years with cross-system architecture ownership for Staff level.
  • You're solid on relational data, including SQL, schema design, transactions, and migrations, and comfortable with modern data platforms: warehouses, pipelines, and getting the right data to the right place.
  • You build with quality and security in mind. That includes testing, accessibility, input validation, authentication and authorization, and common web security risks.
  • You use AI agents for real multi-step work, not just autocomplete. You write clear specs, scope tasks well, give agents the right context, and check what they produce against the real system. Maybe you’ve even said out loud, “I hardly even touch the actual code anymore.”
  • You think like a product engineer. You start with the problem, not the solution, ask "why" before "how," and get creative about solving it.
  • You make thoughtful technical judgments that hold up over time, even while treading in murky waters. You have a bias toward simple, maintainable solutions. KISS or bust.
  • You like thinking out loud. You bring ideas to technical planning, welcome pushback on yours, and give honest, kind feedback in return.
  • You explain decisions, risks, and trade-offs clearly to engineers and non-engineers. You make teammates better through code review, pairing, and mentoring.
  • You've led technical work beyond your own tickets: scoping projects, guiding other engineers, and working with external partners or contractors to keep delivery on track and quality high. At the Staff level, you've owned architecture across multiple systems.
  • You’re curious. You keep up with fast-changing tools and practices, evaluate them on evidence, and know what to bring in and what to admire from afar, based on what we can sustain long-term.

Bonus Points:

  • You've shipped an LLM-backed feature to production and trudged through the task of programmatically determining whether it's doing its job.
  • You've extended an AI development environment with MCP servers, repository instructions, reusable skills, custom workflows, or automated code review.
  • You've worked with business systems like Salesforce, NetSuite, or HRIS platforms.
  • You've built event-driven systems or reverse ETL pipelines.
  • You've worked with AWS or a similar cloud platform, and with infrastructure as code.

jobs.description:
Staff Software Engineer

Location: Remote (U.S.-based) Preference given to CA, TX and FL
Department: Engineering
Reports to: VP of Engineering
Starting Pay Range: $180k - $230k/yr

Company Overview

Work Truck Solutions is the operating system for the commercial vehicle industry. While the retail auto market is saturated with software, the $130B+ commercial truck market was operating in the dark—until we turned on the lights.
We are the only platform that connects the entire ecosystem: OEMs, upfitters, dealerships, and fleet buyers. By digitizing complex inventory data (chassis + upfits) and streamlining the supply chain, we don’t just help dealers sell trucks; we ensure American businesses get the mission-critical vehicles they need to work. We are a team of innovators, disruptors, and problem-solvers dedicated to one mission: removing the friction from the commercial vehicle industry. We are profitable, growing, and aggressively scaling our technology to remain the undisputed authority in this space.

The Role

This is a remote Staff Software Engineer role, our senior individual-contributor track, and the bar is high. A senior engineer is measured by the work they ship; a staff engineer is measured by what the team ships because of them. You are the person others look to when the problem is hard, the requirements are unclear, or the stakes are real. You set technical direction that reaches beyond a single team, choose the patterns others build on, and take the ambiguous, high-impact work that has no obvious owner and drive it to done.
Our engineering team is moving to an agentic way of working, where much of our code is written by AI agents under human review. You will help lead that shift. You know how to build and maintain the skills, agents and context that make AI agents useful on a real codebase, and you set the standards that keep what they produce correct, secure and maintainable. You define how the team builds with AI, not just which tools it uses.
This role is backend focused. You will spend most of your time in .NET and SQL Server, and you will know the frontend well enough to own a feature end to end. You will work day to day inside a software development team of 4-5 engineers, but your influence extends across teams. You make the engineers around you better through the standards you set, the reviews you give, and the way you teach. You have a bias toward action: you would rather ship something real, learn, and correct than debate an abstraction for a week.

Responsibilities

  • Technical leadership across teams. Own the technical direction for your domain and influence it across teams. Make architecture decisions end to end, advocate for the better way to do things, and mentor engineers well beyond your own squad.
  • Lead AI-driven development. Build and maintain the skills, agents, rules and context (such as MCP servers and the documentation agents read) that let the team build with AI. Use AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code or similar) to speed up delivery and to refactor and migrate code at scale.
  • Set the standard for AI-generated code. Define how agent-written pull requests are reviewed and tested, including agentic testing, so that speed does not cost correctness, security or maintainability.
  • Raise the team’s AI fluency. Teach engineers to work this way through pairing, code review and shared tooling. Evaluate new tools and measure whether they actually help.
  • Drive the hard, ambiguous work. Take the projects that lack a clear owner or a clean spec, define the plan and the tradeoffs, and lead them to a shipped result.
  • High-quality output. Build secure, scalable, high-performance applications with a strong focus on maintainability and clean architecture, and set the standard the team builds to.
  • Lead through writing and specs. Write clear technical specifications to frame and lead a project. Establish the performance metrics for your domain, and make sure observability and reliability are designed in, not bolted on.
  • Set and enforce quality. Own coding standards and lead peer code reviews. Use reviews and pairing to teach, not just to gate.
  • Collaboration. Communicate clearly with a distributed team, surface issues early, and work fluently with both technical and non-technical partners.

What We’re Looking For

We are hiring a backend-focused engineer, and .NET is required. You must be expert in .NET (C#, .NET Core, ASP.NET Web API) and SQL Server, with a working foundation in frontend development.
Beyond that depth, we expect:
  • A staff-level track record. Years of building and operating production systems, with a clear history of raising the bar on the teams you have been part of.
  • AI development process experience (required). You know what skills and agents are, and you have built and maintained them for a real codebase and team. You can talk about that work in specifics: skills, agent configurations, rules or MCP integrations you wrote, how you kept them current as the code changed, and a time AI-generated code went wrong and how you caught it. You have a point of view on where these tools help, where they get in the way, and how to review what they produce.
  • Full-stack range. Backend is your home, but you can own a feature from the database to the UI.
  • Strong Git workflow. Branching, pull requests, and code reviews are second nature.

Backend Depth

This is the core of the role.
  • Years of building and operating production-grade systems in .NET (C#, .NET Core, ASP.NET Web API).
  • Demonstrated ownership of scalable, fault-tolerant, performance-critical systems.
  • Strong experience designing API architectures (REST and/or GraphQL) with attention to versioning, maintainability, and real-world tradeoffs.
  • Proven ability to handle complex system challenges, including:
    • Concurrency, data consistency, and race conditions.
    • Caching strategies (Redis, in-memory) and invalidation.
    • Asynchronous processing and queue-based architectures.
  • Deep expertise in SQL Server:
    • Schema design and data modeling.
    • Query optimization, indexing, and performance tuning.
  • Sound judgment on when to use an ORM versus direct SQL.
  • Experience with distributed systems and integrations, including:
    • Event-driven architectures (queues, pub/sub).
    • Resilient integrations (retries, idempotency, failure handling).
  • Strong understanding of security fundamentals (JWT, OAuth, RBAC).
  • Experience with observability and production operations: logging, monitoring, debugging, and root cause analysis.
  • Experience deploying and operating systems in Azure (App Services, Functions, Service Bus, Redis) preferred.
  • Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or similar).

Frontend Foundation

  • Experience building production web applications with React and/or Svelte / SvelteKit.
  • Proficiency in JavaScript and TypeScript.
  • Comfortable with component patterns, application state, and integrating UIs with REST/GraphQL APIs.
  • NodeJS experience is a plus.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building LLM-powered product features, such as tool use, retrieval, or evaluations of AI output.

Benefits

  • Meaningful work on industry-changing products.
  • Competitive salary and a Monday-Friday work week.
  • Excellent medical, dental, 401k, and complimentary life insurance.
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) and paid holidays.
  • Flexible schedule (subject to manager’s discretion).
Work Truck Solutions DOES NOT sponsor H-1B visas.

Along the way, we’ve developed some of the most innovative tools available in analytics, media optimization, reporting, and influencer outreach.

About the Team

The Strategic Analytics Team at BlueLabs drives high quality, innovative research and analysis across BlueLabs’ client sectors, including commercial, political, and non-profit clients, to inform data-driven decisions and strategy. Team members analyze and interpret data, provide strategic program insight, drive innovation across sectors, and collaborate closely with both our client and technical teams.

Our team is often called to answer questions like:

  • What are the meaningful messaging takeaways from a poll of industry elites for a major corporation to consider in their paid communication?
  • How should a movie studio structure their marketing based on who a likely movie goer is?
  • What political trends should a campaign be aware of, and what are the different pathways to victory?
  • How do we present our models, calculators, and reports, so our partners get the information they need?

Tools of the Trade

  • We work closely with our Data Science team, so you’ll need an understanding of statistical concepts, be able to interpret results and explain them to non-analysts
  • We use big data sets so you will need to be comfortable with tools to access information and analyze that information such as SQL and some statistical and/or spreadsheet software
  • We use an array of business intelligence tools to visualize our findings. Members of our team have different strengths such as GIS or Tableau -- so we look for some experience using such tools
  • We’re only successful if we can communicate our findings; writing skills, PowerPoint, Keynote and other tools of the consultant toolbox will help you succeed in this job

As part of the Insights at BlueLabs, you’ll be working with a group of analysts and data scientists who work across BlueLabs’ client sectors, including commercial, political, and non-profit clients, to inform data-driven decisions and strategy.

You’ll be providing team leadership, problem solving challenges, and responsible for ensuring we hit deadlines with insightful and actionable analysis.

Such other reasonable tasks may be assigned by management.

Employee listening is a critical way HR leaders understand their organizations, build trust with employees, and turn feedback into action. You’ll create the long-term strategy for Lattice Engagement and lead the first major iteration of that strategy from discovery through launch. jobs.description:
Senior Media Strategist

Location3 | US Remote

About Location3
Most agencies are built for one brand talking to one audience. We are built for brands that grow through local operators, where the marketing has to work in hundreds of different local markets at once and the people spending the budget are independent owners rather than a corporate team. That is a harder problem, and it is the one we have spent twenty five years on. We also build LOCALACT, the platform those owners use to run their own local marketing.

Position Summary

The Senior Media Strategist owns the strategic direction of paid media programs for Location3's enterprise and multi-location clients. This role sets the why behind every media plan: sizing total addressable markets, building audience cohort profiles, mapping media consumption habits, and translating research into the channel and budget allocations that move client business forward. This role combines media strategy and planning, along with hands-on management of search engine marketing (SEM) campaigns, keeping the strategist close to platform performance and credible in front of clients.

This is a senior, client-facing role. You will build and maintain client playbooks and testing frameworks, present media strategies backed by data-driven insights directly to clients and guide the broader account team on how strategy translates into execution. The right person brings strong strategic and analytical range alongside hands-on SEM expertise while comfortable moving between long-range planning and in-platform work.

What You'll Do

Media Strategy and Planning

  • Lead the development of media strategy for enterprise and multi-location clients, sizing total addressable market (TAM), building audience cohort profiles, and mapping media consumption habits to inform channel selection.
  • Build and maintain client playbooks that document strategic approach, channel mix, budget allocation logic, and testing priorities for each account.
  • Design structured testing frameworks, such as TELO (Test, Evaluate, Learn, Optimize), to validate strategic hypotheses across channels, then translate findings into recommendations that scale across the account portfolio.
  • Set channel and budget allocation recommendations across paid search, paid social, programmatic, display, and video, grounded in audience research and performance data.
  • Translate market research, consumer behavior data, and competitive landscape analysis into clear, actionable strategic direction for clients and internal teams.
  • Present media strategies and performance narratives directly to clients, explaining what happened, why it happened, and what should change next, backed by data-driven insights.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align strategy with execution and with each client's broader marketing objectives.
  • Monitor emerging trends in media consumption and the wider digital advertising landscape, bringing new ideas to clients and to the agency.
  • Elevate the work of junior practitioners by contributing to shared standards, templates, and best practices.

SEM Campaign Management

  • Manage hands-on-keyboard SEM execution across Google (Search, Performance Max, GDN, YouTube, Demand Gen, and Shopping) and Microsoft Ads (Bing), in service of the strategy you set.
  • Own SEM account architecture, bid strategy, keywords, and match types, connecting each lever back to client business goals.
  • Run a disciplined optimization cadence across accounts, diagnosing the root causes behind performance shifts and optimizing bidding, targeting, ad copy, and account structure to protect and improve results.
  • Manage SEM budgets with precision: pacing accurately, anticipating risk before it affects delivery, and reallocating spend to where demand and efficiency are strongest.
  • Report on core SEM metrics (CPA/CPL, ROAS, CVR, impression share) and complete and present paid search audits.
  • Help develop and refine SOPs for SEM tasks and identify opportunities for automation.

What You'll Bring

Strategy and analytical expertise

  • 5-7+ years of experience spanning media strategy and planning and hands-on paid search management, ideally with enterprise or multi-location clients.
  • Demonstrated ability to size total addressable markets, build audience and cohort profiles, and craft compelling narratives that translate research and consumer data into media strategy.
  • Experience building client-facing strategic deliverables such as playbooks, testing frameworks, and channel or budget recommendations.
  • Fluency in core performance metrics (CPA/CPL, ROAS, CAC, CVR, impression share, lost impression share), with a track record of using them to drive strategic decisions, not just report on them.
  • Deep command of SEM fundamentals: keyword strategy, match types, auction dynamics, Smart Bidding, and search term analysis.
  • Experience with GTM, conversion tracking, and data feed management.
  • A holistic understanding of the digital advertising landscape and a habit of staying current on media consumption trends.

How you work

  • You are a confident, polished presenter who can stand in front of clients and translate complex performance data into recommendations that resonate with marketing and executive stakeholders alike.
  • You are proactive. You take ownership and bring an account-first mindset to both strategy and execution.
  • Strategic and execution-minded, comfortable setting direction and doing the in-platform work to bring it to life.
  • Highly organized with strong QA discipline and documentation habits across complex, multi-location account portfolios.
  • A collaborative team member who shares what you're learning and helps junior practitioners grow.

Compensation and benefits

$105,000 to $120,000 base depending on experience, plus commission on new business. This is a full-time, exempt position. Eligible for the annual company bonus, paid on company performance. Medical, dental and vision cover. A 401(k) with company match. Wellbeing stipends, paid time off, and support for remote working.

Salary: $105,000 – $120,000 / year
